bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第197卷卷第一百九十七

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 197, Volume One Hundred Ninety-Seven
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 197

sentences.zh: 【唐紀十三】 趣昭陽單閼四月，盡旃蒙大荒落五月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 13] From the fourth month of the year Quzhaoyang Dan'e through the fifth month of the year Zhanmeng Dahuangluo — in all a little more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 13] Covering from the fourth month of the Quzhaoyang Dan'e cycle year through the fifth month of the Zhanmeng Dahuangluo year — somewhat more than two years in total.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚辰朔，承基上變，告太子謀反。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day of the month (gengchen), Chenji submitted an accusation, reporting that the Crown Prince was plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day (gengchen), Gan Chenji laid an accusation, charging the Crown Prince with treason.

sentences.zh: 敕長孫無忌、房玄齡、蕭瑀、李世勣與大理、中書、門下參鞫之，反形已具。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Xiao Yu, and Li Shiji, together with the Court of Judicial Review, the Secretariat, and the Chancellery, to join in the interrogation; the evidence of rebellion was complete.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Xiao Yu, and Li Shiji, along with the Court of Judicial Review, the Secretariat, and the Chancellery, to investigate jointly; the case for rebellion was fully established.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣：「將何以處承乾？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attendants: "How shall we deal with Chengqian?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his courtiers, "What shall we do with Chengqian?"

sentences.zh: 群臣莫敢對，通事舍人來濟進曰：「陛下不失為慈父，太子得盡天年，則善矣！」

translations.literal: None of the officials dared reply. The Communications Officer Lai Ji stepped forward and said: "If Your Majesty can remain a merciful father and let the Crown Prince live out his natural span, that would be best!"
translations.idiomatic: No one dared answer. The communications officer Lai Ji advanced and said, "If Your Majesty can still be a loving father and let the Crown Prince live out his years, that would be the best outcome!"

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 濟，護兒之子也。

translations.literal: Lai Ji was the son of Lai Hu'er.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Ji was a son of Lai Hu'er.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔廢太子承乾為庶人，幽於右領軍府。

translations.literal: On yiyou, an edict deposed Crown Prince Chengqian as a commoner and confined him in the Right Imperial Guard headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, an edict stripped Crown Prince Chengqian of his rank, reduced him to commoner status, and confined him at the Right Imperial Guard compound.

sentences.zh: 上欲免漢王元昌死，群臣固爭，乃賜自盡於家，而宥其母、妻、子。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to spare Prince of Han Yuanchang from death; the officials pressed their objections firmly, whereupon he was granted permission to take his own life at home, while his mother, wife, and children were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to spare Prince of Han Yuanchang's life, but the ministers argued strenuously until he was allowed to kill himself at home; his mother, wife, and children were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 侯君集、李安儼、趙節、杜荷等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Hou Junji, Li Anyi, Zhao Jie, Du He, and others were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji, Li Anyi, Zhao Jie, Du He, and the rest were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 左庶子張玄素、右庶子趙弘智、令狐德棻等以不能諫爭，皆坐免為庶人。

translations.literal: The Left Subordinate Zhang Xuansu, the Right Subordinate Zhao Hongzhi, Linghu Defen, and others, for failing to remonstrate, were all dismissed and reduced to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right subordinates Zhang Xuansu, Zhao Hongzhi, Linghu Defen, and others, because they had not remonstrated effectively, were all dismissed and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 餘當連坐者，悉赦之。

translations.literal: All others who would have been implicated by association were entirely pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone else who would have been punished by association was fully pardoned.

sentences.zh: 詹事於志寧以數諫，獨蒙勞勉。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor Yu Zhining, for having remonstrated repeatedly, alone received commendation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The grand tutor Yu Zhining alone was praised and encouraged, for having remonstrated again and again.

sentences.zh: 以紇干承基為祐川府折衝都尉，爵平棘縣公。

translations.literal: Gan Chenji was appointed Defender-General of Youchuan Prefecture and enfeoffed as Duke of Pingji County.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Chenji was made Defender-General of Youchuan Prefecture and ennobled as Duke of Pingji County.

sentences.zh: 侯君集被收，賀蘭楚石復詣闕告其事，上引君集謂曰：「朕不欲令刀筆吏辱公，故自鞫公耳。」

translations.literal: When Hou Junji was taken into custody, Helan Chushi again came to the palace to report the matter. The emperor brought Junji forward and said: "I did not wish to let the clerks humiliate you, so I interrogated you myself."
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Junji was arrested, Helan Chushi came again to the palace to report the affair. The emperor had Junji brought before him and said, "I did not want petty clerks to disgrace you, so I questioned you myself."

sentences.zh: 君集初不承。

translations.literal: At first Junji would not confess.
translations.idiomatic: At first Junji denied everything.

sentences.zh: 引楚石具陳始未，又以所與承乾往來啟示之，君集辭窮，乃服。

translations.literal: Chushi was brought in to narrate the whole course of events from beginning to end, and the correspondence between Junji and Chengqian was also shown to him; Junji's arguments were exhausted, and he then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chushi was produced to recount the entire affair from start to finish, and the letters exchanged with Chengqian were shown him as well; with no defense left, Junji finally confessed.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「君集有功，欲乞其生，可乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attendants: "Junji has rendered meritorious service; might we beg his life — would that be permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to his courtiers, "Junji has great achievements to his credit. Could we plead for his life?"

sentences.zh: 群臣以為不可。

translations.literal: The officials all held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all said it was impossible.

sentences.zh: 上乃謂君集曰：「與公長訣矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor then said to Junji: "This is our long farewell!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then told Junji, "This is our final parting!"

sentences.zh: 因泣下，君集亦自投於地；

translations.literal: He wept as he spoke; Junji too threw himself to the ground;
translations.idiomatic: He burst into tears; Junji likewise prostrated himself on the ground;

sentences.zh: 遂斬之於市。

translations.literal: and he was then beheaded in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: and Junji was beheaded in the public square.

sentences.zh: 君集臨刑，謂監刑將軍曰：「君集蹉跌至此！

translations.literal: As Junji faced execution, he said to the supervising general: "Junji has stumbled to this pass!
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, Junji said to the supervising general, "I have fallen this low!

sentences.zh: 然事陛下於籓邸，擊取二國，乞全一子以奉祭祀。」

translations.literal: Yet when I served Your Majesty in the princely residence, I captured two kingdoms; I beg that one son be spared to maintain the sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: Yet when I served Your Majesty in your princely days, I helped conquer two states. I beg you to spare one son to carry on the ancestral rites."

sentences.zh: 上乃原其妻及子，徙嶺南。

translations.literal: The emperor then pardoned his wife and sons and exiled them to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then spared his wife and sons and banished them to the far south.

sentences.zh: 籍沒其家，得二美人，自幼飲人乳而不食。

translations.literal: His household goods were confiscated; among them were two beautiful women who from childhood had been fed on human milk and ate nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: His property was confiscated, and among it were two beauties who since childhood had been nourished on human milk and ate no other food.

sentences.zh: 初，上使李靖教君集兵法，君集言於上曰：「李靖將反矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had Li Jing teach Junji the art of war. Junji said to the emperor: "Li Jing is about to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had Li Jing instruct Junji in military strategy. Junji told the emperor, "Li Jing is going to rebel."

sentences.zh: 上問其故，對曰：「靖獨教臣以其粗而匿其精，以是知之。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason. He replied: "Jing alone taught me only the rough outline and concealed the refinements — from this I know it."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked why, he answered, "Jing taught me only the rough parts and hid the essentials — that is how I know."

sentences.zh: 上以問靖，靖對曰：「此乃君集欲反耳。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Jing about this. Jing replied: "This means Junji himself intends to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Jing, who replied, "That only means Junji himself means to rebel.

sentences.zh: 今諸夏已定，臣之所教，足以制四夷，而君集固求盡臣之術，非反而何！」

translations.literal: Now that all within the realm is settled, what I have taught is sufficient to control the four barbarian quarters, yet Junji insistently demanded to learn all my techniques — if not rebellion, what else!"
translations.idiomatic: Now that the empire is settled, what I have taught is enough to subdue the barbarians on every side, yet Junji kept pressing to learn every last technique of mine — if that is not rebellion, what is it!"

sentences.zh: 江夏王道宗嘗從容言於上曰：「君集志大而智小，自負微功，恥在房玄齡、李靖之下，雖為吏部尚書，未滿其志。

translations.literal: Prince Jiangxia Daozong once said to the emperor at leisure: "Junji's ambitions are large but his wisdom small; he prides himself on slight achievements and is ashamed to rank below Fang Xuanling and Li Jing. Though he is Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, his ambitions are not satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiangxia, Li Daozong, once remarked to the emperor in an unhurried way, "Junji's ambitions outrun his judgment. He takes pride in modest achievements and resents standing below Fang Xuanling and Li Jing. Even as Minister of Personnel, he is not content.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，必將為亂。」

translations.literal: In my view, he will surely bring disorder."
translations.idiomatic: In my judgment, he is bound to make trouble."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「君集材器，亦何施不可！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Junji's talent and capacity — what could he not be assigned to!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "With Junji's talent, what post could he not fill!

sentences.zh: 朕豈惜重位，但次第未至耳，豈可億度，妄生猜貳邪！」

translations.literal: Would I begrudge him a weighty post? It is only that his turn has not yet come. How can one guess at things and recklessly breed suspicion and estrangement!"
translations.idiomatic: Do you think I begrudge him high office? His turn simply has not come yet. How can one speculate idly and breed groundless suspicion!"

sentences.zh: 及君集反誅，上乃謝道宗曰：「果如卿言！」

translations.literal: When Junji rebelled and was executed, the emperor then apologized to Daozong, saying: "It turned out just as you said!"
translations.idiomatic: When Junji was executed for rebellion, the emperor admitted to Daozong, "It happened exactly as you said!"

sentences.zh: 李安儼父，年九十餘，上愍之，賜奴婢以養之。

translations.literal: Li Anyi's father was over ninety years old; the emperor took pity on him and granted slaves and maidservants to support him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Anyi's father was more than ninety; the emperor pitied him and gave him slaves and servants for his upkeep.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾既獲罪，魏王泰日入侍奉，上面許立為太子，岑文本、劉洎亦勸之；

translations.literal: After Crown Prince Chengqian had been found guilty, Prince of Wei Tai came daily to attend upon the emperor. The emperor orally agreed to establish him as crown prince; Cen Wenben and Liu Ji also urged this;
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Chengqian was condemned, Prince of Wei Li Tai attended the emperor every day. The emperor verbally agreed to make him heir, and Cen Wenben and Liu Ji urged it as well;

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌固請立晉王治。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji firmly petitioned to establish Prince of Jin Zhi instead.
translations.idiomatic: but Zhangsun Wuji steadfastly pressed for Prince of Jin Li Zhi.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「昨青雀投我懷云：『臣今日始得為陛下子，乃更生之日也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attendants: "Yesterday Azure Sparrow threw himself into my arms and said: 'Today I have at last become Your Majesty's son in truth — this is a day of rebirth for me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his courtiers, "Yesterday Azure Sparrow threw himself into my arms and said, 'Today I have truly become Your Majesty's son — it is like being born again.

sentences.zh: 臣有一子，臣死之日，當為陛下殺之，傳位晉王。』

translations.literal: I have one son; on the day I die, I shall kill him for Your Majesty and pass the succession to the Prince of Jin.'
translations.idiomatic: I have a son; when I die, I will kill him for Your Majesty and pass the throne to the Prince of Jin.'

sentences.zh: 人誰不愛其子，朕見其如此，甚憐之。」

translations.literal: Who does not love his own son? When I saw him speak thus, I felt deep pity for him."
translations.idiomatic: Who does not love his own child? When I saw him speak this way, I was deeply moved."

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫褚遂良曰：「陛下言大失。

translations.literal: The Remonstrance Officer Chu Suiliang said: "Your Majesty's words are gravely mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance officer Chu Suiliang said, "Your Majesty has spoken very wrongly.

sentences.zh: 願審思，勿誤也！

translations.literal: I beg you to consider carefully and not err!
translations.idiomatic: Please think this through carefully and do not go astray!

sentences.zh: 安有陛下萬歲後，魏王據天下，肯殺其愛子，傳位晉王者乎！

translations.literal: How could there be, after Your Majesty's ten thousand years, a Prince of Wei holding all under Heaven who would be willing to kill his beloved son and pass the throne to the Prince of Jin!
translations.idiomatic: After Your Majesty's death, when the Prince of Wei holds the realm, would he truly kill his own beloved son and hand the throne to the Prince of Jin!

sentences.zh: 陛下日者既立承乾為太子，復寵魏王，禮秩過於承乾，以成今日之禍。

translations.literal: Your Majesty once established Chengqian as crown prince, then again favored the Prince of Wei, whose ceremonial rank exceeded Chengqian's — and so brought about today's calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty first made Chengqian crown prince, then favored the Prince of Wei above measure, giving him honors that surpassed the heir — and that is how today's disaster came about.

sentences.zh: 前事不遠，足以為鑒。

translations.literal: The recent past is not far off and is warning enough.
translations.idiomatic: Recent events are still fresh — they are warning enough.

sentences.zh: 陛下今立魏王，願先措置晉王，始得安全耳。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty now establishes the Prince of Wei, I beg you first to make arrangements for the Prince of Jin — only then will he be safe."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty now makes the Prince of Wei heir, you must first settle the Prince of Jin's position — only then will he be safe."

sentences.zh: 上流涕曰：「我不能爾！」

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: "I cannot do that!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, "I cannot do that!"

sentences.zh: 因起，入宮。

translations.literal: He then rose and entered the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose and withdrew to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 魏王泰恐上立晉王治，謂之曰：「汝與元昌善，元昌今敗，得無憂乎？」

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Tai, fearing that the emperor would establish Prince of Jin Zhi, said to him: "You were on good terms with Yuanchang; Yuanchang has now fallen — are you not worried?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Li Tai, fearing the emperor would name Prince of Jin Li Zhi heir, said to him, "You were close to Yuanchang; Yuanchang has fallen — shouldn't you be worried?"

sentences.zh: 治由是憂形於色，上怪，屢問其故，治乃以狀告；

translations.literal: From this Zhi showed worry in his countenance. The emperor was puzzled and repeatedly asked the reason; Zhi then reported the whole affair;
translations.idiomatic: From this Zhi's distress showed plainly on his face. The emperor noticed and asked repeatedly what was wrong; Zhi then told him what had happened;

sentences.zh: 上憮然，始悔立泰之言矣。

translations.literal: the emperor was downcast and began to regret his words about establishing Tai.
translations.idiomatic: and the emperor, stricken, began to regret having spoken of making Tai heir.

sentences.zh: 上面責承乾，承乾曰：「臣為太子，復何所求！

translations.literal: The emperor personally reproached Chengqian. Chengqian said: "As crown prince, what more could I seek!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor confronted Chengqian in person. Chengqian said, "As crown prince, what more could I want!

sentences.zh: 但為泰所圖，時與朝臣謀自安之術，不逞之人遂教臣為不軌耳。

translations.literal: It was only that Tai plotted against me; I often consulted court officials on means to secure myself, and unscrupulous men then taught me unlawful courses.
translations.idiomatic: It was only that Tai was plotting against me; I often discussed with court officials how to protect myself, and wicked men then urged me into treason.

sentences.zh: 今若泰為太子，所謂落其度內。」

translations.literal: If Tai is now made crown prince, that is precisely what he calls falling within his measure."
translations.idiomatic: If Tai becomes crown prince now, that is exactly what he has been scheming for all along."

sentences.zh: 承乾既廢，上御兩儀殿，群臣俱出，獨留長孫無忌、房玄齡、李世勣、褚遂良，謂曰：「我三子一弟，所為如是，我心誠無聊賴！」

translations.literal: After Chengqian was deposed, the emperor took the throne in the Hall of Two Principles. When all the officials had withdrawn, he kept only Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Shiji, and Chu Suiliang, and said: "My three sons and one younger brother have acted thus — my heart is truly without comfort!"
translations.idiomatic: After Chengqian was deposed, the emperor held court in the Hall of Two Principles. When the other officials had left, he kept only Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Shiji, and Chu Suiliang and said, "My three sons and one brother have behaved like this — my heart is utterly worn out!"

sentences.zh: 因自投於床，無忌等爭前扶抱；

translations.literal: He then threw himself upon the couch; Wuji and the others rushed forward to support him;
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself on the couch; Wuji and the others rushed forward to hold him up;

sentences.zh: 上又抽佩刀欲自刺，遂良奪刀以授晉王治。

translations.literal: the emperor again drew his girdle dagger intending to stab himself; Suiliang seized the blade and handed it to Prince of Jin Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor drew his dagger to stab himself; Suiliang wrested it away and gave it to Prince of Jin Li Zhi.

sentences.zh: 無忌等請上所欲，上曰：「我欲立晉王。」

translations.literal: Wuji and the others asked what the emperor wished. He said: "I wish to establish the Prince of Jin."
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and the others asked what he wanted. He said, "I wish to make the Prince of Jin my heir."

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「謹奉詔；

translations.literal: Wuji said: "We respectfully receive the edict;
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said, "We accept Your Majesty's command;

sentences.zh: 有異議者，臣請斬之！」

translations.literal: whoever raises objection, your servant asks leave to behead him!"
translations.idiomatic: anyone who objects, I ask leave to execute!"

sentences.zh: 上謂治曰：「汝舅許汝矣，宜拜謝。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Zhi: "Your uncle has agreed for you; you should bow in thanks."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Zhi, "Your uncle has agreed — you should bow in gratitude."

sentences.zh: 治因拜之。

translations.literal: Zhi thereupon bowed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi bowed to Wuji.

sentences.zh: 上謂無忌等曰：「公等已同我意，未知外議何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wuji and the others: "You gentlemen already share my intent; I do not know what outside opinion will be like."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Wuji and the others, "You already agree with me — but what will opinion outside the palace be?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「晉王仁孝，天下屬心久矣，乞陛下試召問百官，有不同者，臣負陛下萬死。」

translations.literal: They replied: "The Prince of Jin is benevolent and filial; the hearts of all under Heaven have long been turned to him. We beg Your Majesty to try summoning the hundred officials and questioning them — if there is any dissent, your servant will accept ten thousand deaths at Your Majesty's hands."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "The Prince of Jin is benevolent and filial; the empire has long looked to him. Please summon the officials and ask them — if anyone disagrees, I deserve death a thousand times over."

sentences.zh: 上乃御太極殿，召文武六品以上，謂曰：「承乾悖逆，泰亦凶險，皆不可立。

translations.literal: The emperor then took the throne in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, summoned civil and military officials of the sixth rank and above, and said: "Chengqian was rebellious and Tai is dangerous as well — neither may be established.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then held court in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, summoned all civil and military officials of the sixth rank and above, and said, "Chengqian was treasonous and Tai is treacherous — neither can be heir.

sentences.zh: 朕欲選諸子為嗣，誰可者？

translations.literal: I wish to choose among my sons for the succession — who is suitable?
translations.idiomatic: I wish to choose one of my sons as heir — who is fit?

sentences.zh: 卿輩明言之。」

translations.literal: Speak plainly, all of you."
translations.idiomatic: Speak your minds plainly."

sentences.zh: 眾皆歡呼曰：「晉王仁孝，當為嗣。」

translations.literal: All cried out together: "The Prince of Jin is benevolent and filial — he should be the successor."
translations.idiomatic: All shouted as one, "The Prince of Jin is benevolent and filial — he should be heir."

sentences.zh: 上悅，是日，泰從百餘騎至永安門；

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased. That same day Tai came with more than a hundred mounted followers to the Gate of Eternal Peace;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased. That day Tai arrived at the Gate of Eternal Peace with more than a hundred horsemen;

sentences.zh: 敕門司盡辟其騎，引泰入肅章門，幽於北苑。

translations.literal: the emperor ordered the gate officials to dismiss all his riders, led Tai in through the Gate of Solemn Regulations, and confined him in the Northern Park.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered the gatekeepers to send away all his escort, had Tai brought in through the Gate of Solemn Regulations, and confined him in the Northern Park.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔立晉王治為皇太子，御承天門樓，赦天下，酺三日。

translations.literal: On bingxu, an edict established Prince of Jin Zhi as crown prince. The emperor took the tower of the Gate of Receiving Heaven, pardoned all under Heaven, and granted three days of public feasting.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, an edict named Prince of Jin Li Zhi crown prince. The emperor appeared on the tower of the Gate of Receiving Heaven, proclaimed a general amnesty, and ordered three days of celebration.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「我若立泰，則是太子之位可經營而得。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attendants: "If I had established Tai, then the position of crown prince could have been obtained by scheming.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his courtiers, "If I had made Tai heir, it would mean the crown prince's place could be won by intrigue.

sentences.zh: 自今太子失道，籓王窺伺者，皆兩棄之，傳諸子孫，永為後法。

translations.literal: From now on, when a crown prince loses the Way and a feudal prince watches for an opening, both shall be cast aside. Let this be handed down to posterity as a perpetual precedent.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whenever an heir goes astray and a prince of the blood watches for his chance, both are to be discarded. Let this be passed down to our descendants as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 且泰立，則承乾與治皆不全；

translations.literal: Moreover, if Tai were established, then Chengqian and Zhi would both be unsafe;
translations.idiomatic: If Tai were made heir, Chengqian and Zhi would both be in peril;

sentences.zh: 治立，則承乾與泰皆無恙矣。」

translations.literal: if Zhi is established, then Chengqian and Tai will both be unharmed."
translations.idiomatic: but with Zhi as heir, Chengqian and Tai will both come to no harm."

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：唐太宗不以天下大器私其所愛，以杜禍亂之原，可謂能遠謀矣！

translations.literal: Your servant Guang remarks: Emperor Taizong of Tang did not treat the great vessel of all under Heaven as a private gift to those he loved, but cut off the source of calamity and disorder — this may be called far-sighted planning!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: Emperor Taizong did not treat the empire as a private gift to a favorite son, but blocked the source of turmoil — truly far-sighted statesmanship!

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以中書令楊師道為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Yang Shidao, Grand Counselor of the Secretariat, was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Grand Counselor Yang Shidao was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 初，長廣公主適趙慈景，生節；

translations.literal: Earlier, Princess Changguang had been married to Zhao Cijing and bore Jie;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Princess Changguang had married Zhao Cijing and borne Zhao Jie;

sentences.zh: 慈景死，更適師道。

translations.literal: after Cijing died she remarried Shidao.
translations.idiomatic: after Cijing died she married Shidao.

sentences.zh: 師道與長孫無忌等共鞫承乾獄，陰為趙節道地，由是獲譴。

translations.literal: Shidao, together with Zhangsun Wuji and others, jointly investigated Chengqian's case and secretly made excuses for Zhao Jie; for this he was censured.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao had joined Zhangsun Wuji and others in investigating Chengqian's case and had secretly pleaded Zhao Jie's cause; for this he was punished.

sentences.zh: 上至公主所，公主以首擊地，泣謝子罪，上亦拜泣曰：「賞不避仇讎，罰不阿親戚，此天下至公之道，不敢違也，以是負姊。」

translations.literal: The emperor went to the princess's residence. The princess beat her head upon the ground, weeping and begging forgiveness for her son's crime. The emperor too bowed and wept, saying: "Rewards do not avoid one's enemies; punishments do not favor one's kin — this is the supreme fairness of all under Heaven. I dare not violate it, and so I have failed you, Elder Sister."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went to the princess's residence. She beat her head on the ground, weeping and begging forgiveness for her son. The emperor bowed and wept as well, saying, "Rewards do not shun one's enemies, and punishments do not favor one's kin — that is the supreme fairness of the realm. I dare not break it, and so I have failed you, Elder Sister."

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔以長孫無忌為太子太師，房玄齡為太傅，蕭瑀為太保，李世勣為詹事，瑀、世勣並同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: On jichou, an edict appointed Zhangsun Wuji as Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, Fang Xuanling as Grand Tutor, Xiao Yu as Grand Protector, and Li Shiji as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Yu and Shiji were both made Associates of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, an edict named Zhangsun Wuji Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, Fang Xuanling Grand Tutor, Xiao Yu Grand Protector, and Li Shiji Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Yu and Shiji were both given the concurrent title of Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 同中書門下三品自此始。

translations.literal: The title Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: The concurrent rank of Associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank dates from this appointment.

sentences.zh: 又以左衛大將軍李大亮領右衛率，前詹事於志寧、中書侍郎馬周為左庶子，吏部侍郎蘇勖、中書舍人高季輔為右庶子，刑部侍郎張行成為少詹事，諫議大夫褚遂良為賓客。

translations.literal: Li Daliang, General of the Left Guard, was also made Commandant of the Right Guard; the former Grand Tutor Yu Zhining and Vice Director of the Secretariat Ma Zhou were made Left Subordinates; Vice Minister of Personnel Su Xu and Secretariat Drafting Officer Gao Jifu were made Right Subordinates; Vice Minister of Justice Zhang Xingcheng was made Junior Grand Tutor; and Remonstrance Officer Chu Suiliang was made Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: General Li Daliang of the Left Guard was also made commandant of the Right Guard; former grand tutor Yu Zhining and vice director Ma Zhou were named left subordinates; vice minister Su Xu and drafting officer Gao Jifu were named right subordinates; vice minister Zhang Xingcheng was made junior grand tutor; and remonstrance officer Chu Suiliang was made guest of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 李世勣嘗得暴疾，方云「須灰可療」；

translations.literal: Li Shiji once suffered a sudden severe illness; the prescription said "ashes are needed for a cure";
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji once fell gravely ill; the prescription called for ashes as medicine;

sentences.zh: 上自剪須，為之和藥。

translations.literal: the emperor himself cut off his beard and mixed the medicine with it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor cut off his own beard and mixed it into the medicine.

sentences.zh: 世勣頓首出血泣謝。

translations.literal: Shiji bowed his head until it bled and wept in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji bowed until his forehead bled and wept his thanks.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「為社稷，非為卿也，何謝之有！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is for the altars of state, not for you personally — what is there to thank!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is for the realm, not for you alone — why thank me?"

sentences.zh: 世勣嘗侍宴，上從容謂曰：「朕求群臣可托幼孤者，無以逾公，公往不負李密，豈負朕哉！」

translations.literal: Once when Shiji was attending a banquet, the emperor said to him at leisure: "Among all my ministers I seek one to whom I may entrust a young orphan — none surpasses you. You did not fail Li Mi in the past; would you fail me!"
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet the emperor said to him in an easy tone, "I have searched among my ministers for one to whom I could entrust a young heir — none surpasses you. You did not betray Li Mi; would you betray me?"

sentences.zh: 世勣流涕辭謝，嚙指出血，因飲沉醉；

translations.literal: Shiji wept and declined with thanks, bit his finger until it bled, and then drank until he was deeply drunk;
translations.idiomatic: Shiji wept and protested his unworthiness, bit his finger until it bled, and then drank himself into a stupor;

sentences.zh: 上解御服以覆之。

translations.literal: "the emperor removed his imperial robe and covered him with it."
translations.idiomatic: "the emperor took off his own robe and laid it over him."

sentences.zh: 癸巳，詔解魏王泰雍州牧、相州都督、左武侯大將軍，降爵為東萊郡王。

translations.literal: On guisi, an edict relieved Prince of Wei Tai of his posts as Governor of Yongzhou, Commander of Xiangzhou, and General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard, and reduced his rank to Prince of Donglai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, an edict stripped Prince of Wei Li Tai of his posts as governor of Yongzhou, commander of Xiangzhou, and general-in-chief of the Left Martial Guard, and reduced him to Prince of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 泰府僚屬為泰所親狎者，皆遷嶺表；

translations.literal: The staff of Tai's princely establishment who had been intimate with him were all exiled beyond the Ling range;
translations.idiomatic: The officials of Tai's household whom he had favored were all banished to the far south;

sentences.zh: 以杜楚客兄如晦有功，免死，廢為庶子。

translations.literal: because Du Chuke's elder brother Ruhui had rendered meritorious service, he was spared death and demoted to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chuke was spared execution because his elder brother Ruhui had earned great merit, but was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 給事中崔仁師嘗密請立魏王泰為太子，左遷鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: Attendant Within Cui Renshi once secretly requested that Prince of Wei Li Tai be installed as crown prince; he was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Renshi, Attendant Within, had once secretly petitioned to make Prince of Wei Li Tai crown prince; for this he was demoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 庚子，定太子見三師儀：迎於殿門外，先拜，三師答拜；

translations.literal: On gengzi, the protocol for the crown prince's audience with the Three Preceptors was fixed: he would receive them outside the palace gate, bow first, and the Three Preceptors would return the bow;
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, regulations were set for how the crown prince was to receive the Three Preceptors: he would meet them outside the palace gate, bow first, and the Three Preceptors would bow in return;

sentences.zh: 每門讓於三師。

translations.literal: At each gate he would yield precedence to the Three Preceptors.
translations.idiomatic: At every gate he would defer to the Three Preceptors.

sentences.zh: 三師坐，太子乃坐。

translations.literal: Only after the Three Preceptors were seated would the crown prince sit.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince would not sit until the Three Preceptors had taken their seats.

sentences.zh: 其與三師書，前後稱名、「惶恐」。

translations.literal: In letters to the Three Preceptors, he would sign his name at the beginning and end and use the term "awe-stricken."
translations.idiomatic: In correspondence with the Three Preceptors, he would sign his own name at the beginning and end and add the deferential phrase "awe-stricken."

sentences.zh: 五月，癸酉，太子上表，以「承乾、泰衣服不過隨身，飲食不能適口，幽憂可愍，乞敕有司，優加供給。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guiyou, the crown prince submitted a memorial stating: "Chengqian and Tai have no more clothing than what they carry on their persons and cannot eat to their satisfaction; their hidden grief is pitiable — I beg that Your Majesty instruct the relevant offices to favor them with additional provisions."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guiyou, the crown prince memorialized the throne, writing that Chengqian and Tai possessed only the clothes on their backs, could not eat properly, and lived in such concealed sorrow as to inspire pity; he asked the emperor to order the responsible officials to grant them generous additional support.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: "The emperor assented."
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor approved the request."

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎劉洎上言，以「太子宜勤學問，親師友。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Liu Ji submitted a memorial stating: "The crown prince ought to apply himself diligently to learning and stay close to his teachers and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Liu Ji memorialized the throne, arguing that the crown prince should study hard and cultivate close ties with his teachers and friends.

sentences.zh: 今入侍宮闈，動逾旬朔，師保以下，接對甚希，伏願少抑下流之愛，弘遠大之規，則海內幸甚！」

translations.literal: Now, in attending within the inner palace, he often goes more than ten days or a full month without meeting the tutors and guardians below them — how rarely he sees them! I humbly wish that Your Majesty would slightly restrain this indulgence of lower affections and enlarge a far-reaching plan; then all within the seas would be fortunate indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet now, dwelling in attendance within the inner palace, he often goes weeks or even a month at a stretch; his tutors and guardians below them seldom receive audience from him. I humbly ask Your Majesty to curb this indulgence of private attachment and instead promote a broader vision — then the realm would be greatly blessed!"

sentences.zh: 上乃命洎與岑文本、褚遂良、馬周更日詣東宮，與太子游處談論。

translations.literal: "The emperor thereupon ordered Liu Ji, together with Cen Wenti, Chu Suiliang, and Ma Zhou, to visit the Eastern Palace on alternate days and spend time with the crown prince in conversation and discussion.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor then ordered Liu Ji, Cen Wenti, Chu Suiliang, and Ma Zhou to take turns visiting the Eastern Palace daily to spend time with the crown prince in conversation and debate.

sentences.zh: 六月，己卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day of the month (jimao), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jimao—the first day of the month—there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，太常丞鄧素使高麗還，請於懷遠鎮增戍兵以逼高麗。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Deng Su, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, returned from a mission to Goguryeo and requested that garrison troops at Huaiyuan garrison be increased to press Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Deng Su returned from a mission to Goguryeo and proposed increasing garrison forces at Huaiyuan to pressure Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「『遠人不服，則修文德以來之』。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "'When distant peoples do not submit, then cultivate civil virtue to draw them in.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "As the saying goes, 'When distant peoples do not submit, cultivate civil virtue to win them over.

sentences.zh: 未聞一二百戍兵能威絕域者也！」

translations.literal: I have never heard that one or two hundred garrison soldiers could awe a distant frontier!"
translations.idiomatic: I have never heard of one or two hundred border garrison troops intimidating a far-off kingdom!"

sentences.zh: 丁酉，右僕射高士廉遜位，許之，其開府儀同三司、勳封如故，仍同門下中書三品，知政事。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Right Vice Director Gao Shilian resigned his post; permission was granted. His Grand Preceptor of the State with Honorary Three Excellencies of the First Rank and his titles of merit and enfeoffment remained unchanged; he still ranked as Third Rank at the Gate and Secretariat and managed state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Right Vice Director Gao Shilian requested retirement, and the emperor granted it. He retained his rank as Grand Preceptor of the State with Honorary Three Excellencies of the First Rank along with his titles of merit and enfeoffment, and continued to serve at Third Rank in the Gate and Secretariat, managing affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 閏月，辛亥，上謂侍臣曰：「朕自立太子，遇物則誨之，見其飯，則曰：『汝知稼穡之艱難，則常有斯飯矣。』

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on xinhai, the emperor said to his attending ministers: "Since I installed the crown prince, whenever I encounter something I instruct him. When I see him at a meal, I say: 'If you know how arduous grain cultivation is, you will always have this rice.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on xinhai, Emperor Taizong told his ministers, "Since establishing the crown prince, I take every opportunity to instruct him. When I see him eating, I say: 'Know the hardship of tilling and sowing, and you will never lack this meal.

sentences.zh: 見其乘馬，則曰：『汝知其勞逸，不竭其力，則常得乘之矣。』

translations.literal: When I see him riding a horse, I say: 'If you know its labors and rest and do not exhaust its strength, you can always ride it.'"
translations.idiomatic: When I see him on horseback, I say: 'Understand a horse's labor and rest; do not exhaust its strength, and you will always have a mount.'"

sentences.zh: 見其乘舟，則曰：『水所以載舟，亦所以覆舟，民猶水也，君猶舟也。』

translations.literal: When I see him on a boat, I say: 'Water is what carries the boat and also what capsizes it; the people are like water, the ruler is like the boat.'"
translations.idiomatic: When I see him aboard a boat, I say: 'Water bears the boat up, but it also overturns it — the people are the water, and the ruler is the boat.'"

sentences.zh: 見其息於木下，則曰：『木從繩則正，後從諫則聖。』」

translations.literal: When I see him resting beneath a tree, I say: 'Wood made to follow the line is straight; the ruler who follows remonstrance becomes sage.'"
translations.idiomatic: When I see him resting under a tree, I say: 'Timber that follows the carpenter's line is straight; a ruler who heeds remonstrance becomes a sage.'"

sentences.zh: 丁巳，詔太子知左、右屯營兵馬事，其大將軍以下並受處分。

translations.literal: On dingsi, an edict ordered the crown prince to oversee the military affairs of the Left and Right Garrison Camps; all officers below the grand generals were to receive his orders.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, an edict appointed the crown prince to manage the horse and troop affairs of the Left and Right Garrison Camps, with all officers below the grand generals subject to his command.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀真珠可汗使其侄突利設來納幣，獻馬五萬匹，牛、橐駝萬頭，羊十萬口。

translations.literal: Xueyantuo Khan Zhenzhu sent his nephew Tuli She to present betrothal gifts, offering fifty thousand horses, ten thousand head of cattle and camels, and one hundred thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhu Khan of the Xueyantuo sent his nephew Tuli She with betrothal gifts: fifty thousand horses, ten thousand cattle and camels, and one hundred thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 庚申，突利設獻饌，上御相思殿，大饗群臣，設十部樂，突利設再拜上壽，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Tuli She presented a feast; the emperor attended at Xiangsi Hall, gave a great banquet to the assembled ministers, set out ten sections of music; Tuli She bowed twice and offered a toast to long life; gifts and rewards were extremely generous.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Tuli She presented a banquet. Emperor Taizong received him at Xiangsi Hall and held a grand feast for his ministers with ten-part music. Tuli She bowed twice and offered a toast for the emperor's longevity, and the rewards lavished upon him were lavish indeed.

sentences.zh: 契苾何力上言：「薛延陀不可與昏。」

translations.literal: Qibi Heli submitted a memorial: "One must not marry into Xueyantuo."
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heli memorialized the throne: "We must not marry the princess to Xueyantuo."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吾已許之矣，豈可為天子而食言乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have already promised this — how can a Son of Heaven go back on his word!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I have already given my word — how can a Son of Heaven break a promise!"

sentences.zh: 何力對曰：「臣非欲陛下遽絕之也，願且遷延其事。

translations.literal: Qibi Heli replied: "Your servant does not wish Your Majesty to break it off at once; I hope only to delay the matter for now.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heli answered, "I do not ask Your Majesty to sever the match immediately — only to delay it for the time being.

sentences.zh: 臣聞古有親迎之禮，若敕夷男使親迎，雖不至京師，亦應至靈州；

translations.literal: I have heard that antiquity had the rite of the bridegroom going in person to greet the bride. If Your Majesty orders Yinan to come in person to greet her, though he need not reach the capital, he ought at least to come to Lingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity there was a custom requiring the bridegroom to fetch the bride in person. If Your Majesty orders Yinan to come and greet her himself — he need not reach the capital, but he should at least come to Lingzhou —

sentences.zh: 彼必不敢來，則絕之有名矣。

translations.literal: he will surely not dare come, and then to break off the marriage will have grounds.
translations.idiomatic: he will certainly not dare come, and we will then have good reason to dissolve the alliance.

sentences.zh: 夷男性剛戾，既不成昏，其下復攜貳，不過一二年必病死，二爭立，則可以坐制之矣！」

translations.literal: Yinan is by nature fierce and obstinate. Once the marriage fails, his subordinates will again become divided in loyalty; in no more than a year or two he will surely die of illness, and when two contend for the succession, then we can control them without lifting a hand!"
translations.idiomatic: Yinan is fierce and intractable. Once the marriage falls through, his followers will turn disloyal again; within a year or two he will die of illness, and when his sons fight for the succession, we can dominate them without effort!"

sentences.zh: 上從之，乃征真珠可汁使親迎，仍發詔將幸靈州與之會。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice and summoned Khan Zhenzhu to come in person to greet the bride; he also issued an edict that he would travel to Lingzhou to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and summoned Zhenzhu Khan to fetch the bride in person, while issuing an edict announcing his own intended visit to Lingzhou for the meeting.

sentences.zh: 真珠大喜，欲詣靈州，其臣諫曰：「脫為所留，悔之無及！」

translations.literal: Zhenzhu was greatly pleased and wished to go to Lingzhou. His ministers remonstrated, saying: "If by chance you are detained there, regret will come too late!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhu was overjoyed and prepared to go to Lingzhou. His ministers warned him: "If they detain you, it will be too late for regret!"

sentences.zh: 真珠曰：「吾聞唐天子有聖德，我得身往見之，死無所恨，且漠北必當有主。

translations.literal: Zhenzhu said: "I have heard that the Tang Son of Heaven possesses sagely virtue. If I can go in person to see him, I will die without regret — moreover, the north of the desert must surely have its lord.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhu replied, "I have heard the Tang emperor is a sage. To meet him face to face, I would die content — and in any case, the northern steppe must have its master.

sentences.zh: 我行決矣，勿復多言！」

translations.literal: My journey is decided — speak no more of this!"
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up — say no more!"

sentences.zh: 上發使三道，受其所獻雜蓄。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys along three routes to receive the livestock and goods he presented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys along three routes to accept the livestock and goods offered in tribute.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀先天庫廄，真珠調斂諸部，往返萬里，道涉沙磧，無水草，耗死將半，失期不至。

translations.literal: Xueyantuo had lacked granaries and stables from the first; Zhenzhu levied upon the various tribes, and the round trip of ten thousand li crossed sandy wastes without grass or water — nearly half died on the road; he missed the deadline and did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo had never maintained granaries or stables. Zhenzhu requisitioned supplies from every tribe; the ten-thousand-li journey crossed barren deserts without grass or water, and nearly half the animals perished en route. He missed the appointed date and failed to arrive.

sentences.zh: 議者或以為聘財未備而與為昏，將使戎狄輕中國，上乃下詔絕其昏，停幸靈州，追還三使。

translations.literal: Some at court argued that to marry her when the betrothal gifts were not complete would make the barbarians look down on China. The emperor thereupon issued an edict breaking off the marriage, canceled the planned visit to Lingzhou, and recalled the three envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Some officials argued that marrying the princess when betrothal gifts were incomplete would make the frontier peoples despise China. The emperor issued an edict canceling the marriage, aborted his journey to Lingzhou, and recalled the three envoys.

sentences.zh: 褚遂良上疏，以為：「薛延陀本一俟斤，陛下蕩平沙塞，萬里蕭條，餘寇奔波，須有酋長，璽書鼓纛，立為可汗。

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial, stating: "Xueyantuo was originally a mere irkin; Your Majesty swept the sandy frontier clean, and for ten thousand li all was desolate. The remnant bandits fled in panic — a chieftain was needed; with imperial seal and military banners he was installed as khan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial arguing that Xueyantuo had originally been only an irkin chieftain; after Your Majesty pacified the desert frontier, leaving ten thousand li barren, the surviving raiders needed a leader — so Your Majesty invested him as khan with imperial patent and banners.

sentences.zh: 比者復降鴻私，許其姻媾，西告吐蕃，北諭思摩，中國童幼，靡不知之。

translations.literal: Recently Your Majesty again bestowed great private favor, agreeing to a marriage alliance; this was announced west to Tibet and north to Ishbara; even Chinese children knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Your Majesty again showed extraordinary favor, consenting to a marriage alliance — announced west to Tibet and north to Ishbara, so that even children within China knew of it.

sentences.zh: 御幸北門，受其獻食，群臣四夷，宴樂終日。

translations.literal: Your Majesty went in person to the Northern Gate to accept his offerings of food; ministers and the four barbarian peoples feasted and made merry the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty personally attended the Northern Gate to accept his offerings; ministers and foreign envoys feasted together throughout the day.

sentences.zh: 鹹言陛下欲安百姓，不愛一女，凡在含生，孰不懷德。

translations.literal: All declared that Your Majesty wished to secure the people's peace and did not grudge a single daughter; every living thing — who would not cherish such virtue?
translations.idiomatic: All proclaimed that Your Majesty sought the people's peace and did not begrudge a daughter — what living soul would not revere such virtue?

sentences.zh: 今一朝生進退之意，有改悔之心，臣為國家惜茲聲聽；

translations.literal: Now, in a single morning, to show intention of advancing or retreating, to harbor a mind of regret — your servant grieves for the nation's reputation on your behalf;
translations.idiomatic: To change course overnight and show second thoughts — I mourn what this will cost our nation's standing;

sentences.zh: 所顧甚少，所失殊多，嫌隙既生，必構邊患。

translations.literal: what is considered is small, what is lost is great; once suspicion and rift arise, border troubles will surely follow.
translations.idiomatic: the gain is slight, the loss enormous; once enmity takes root, border troubles are inevitable.

sentences.zh: 彼國蓄見欺之怒，此民懷負約之慚，恐非所以服遠人、訓戎士也。

translations.literal: That country will harbor the rage of being deceived; this people will bear the shame of breaking faith — I fear this is not the way to subdue distant peoples or instruct frontier warriors.
translations.idiomatic: They will nurture the fury of deception; our people will feel the shame of broken faith — this is no way to win distant peoples or instruct our frontier troops.

sentences.zh: 陛下君臨天下十有七載，以仁恩結庶類，以信義撫戎夷，莫不欣然，負之無力，何惜不使有始有卒乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ruled the realm for seventeen years, binding all classes with benevolence and kindness, soothing the barbarians with faith and righteousness — all have rejoiced; they cannot bear up against you in strength — why begrudge finishing what was begun?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has ruled for seventeen years, uniting the people through benevolence and winning the barbarians through faith — all rejoice, and none can resist you. Why not see this through to the end?

sentences.zh: 夫龍沙以北，部落無算，中國誅之，終不能盡，當懷之以德，使為惡者在夷不在華，失信者在彼不在此，則堯、舜、禹、湯不及陛下遠矣！」

translations.literal: North of the Dragon Sands, tribes are countless; if China slaughters them, they can never all be exterminated — one ought to embrace them with virtue, so that those who do evil lie among the barbarians, not among the Chinese, and those who break faith lie over there, not over here — then Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang would not equal Your Majesty by far!"
translations.idiomatic: North of the Dragon Sands lie innumerable tribes; China cannot slaughter them all. Win them with virtue, so that wrongdoers are among the barbarians, not the Chinese, and oath-breakers are on their side, not ours — then even Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang would pale before Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 上不聽。

translations.literal: "The emperor did not heed this.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 是時，群臣多言：「國家既許其昏，受其聘幣，不可失信戎狄，更生邊患。」

translations.literal: At this time many among the ministers said: "The state has already promised the marriage and accepted the betrothal gifts — faith cannot be broken with the barbarians, lest new border troubles arise."
translations.idiomatic: Many ministers argued that since the state had promised the marriage and accepted the gifts, breaking faith with the barbarians would invite fresh border trouble.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿曹皆知古而不知今。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You all know antiquity but not the present.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "You understand the past but not the present.

sentences.zh: 昔漢初匈奴強，中國弱，故飾子女、捐金絮以餌之，得事之宜。

translations.literal: In former times, at the beginning of Han, the Xiongnu were strong and China weak, so they adorned daughters with gifts and sent gold and silk to entice them — obtaining what suited the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: In early Han times the Xiongnu were mighty and China weak, so she dressed up princesses and sent gold and silk as tribute — that suited the times.

sentences.zh: 今中國強，戎狄弱，以我徒兵一千，可擊胡騎數萬。

translations.literal: Now China is strong and the barbarians weak; with a thousand foot soldiers of ours we can strike tens of thousands of Hun cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Today China is strong and the frontier peoples weak — a thousand of our infantry can attack tens of thousands of nomad horsemen.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀所以匍匐稽顙，惟我所欲，不敢驕慢者，以新為君長，雜姓非其種族，欲假中國之勢以威服之耳。

translations.literal: The reason Xueyantuo crawls and kowtows, yielding to whatever I wish and not daring to be arrogant, is that he has newly become chieftain, the mixed surnames are not his tribe, and he wishes to borrow China's prestige to awe them into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo grovels and kowtows, yielding to my every wish and never daring arrogance, because he is a newly installed chieftain whose mixed tribes are not of his own lineage — he needs China's backing to intimidate them.

sentences.zh: 彼同羅、僕骨、回紇等十餘部，兵各數萬，並力攻之，立可破滅，所以不敢發者，畏中國所立故也。

translations.literal: Those Tongluo, Pugu, Uighur, and more than ten other tribes, each with armies of tens of thousands — combined they could attack and destroy him at once; the reason they dare not move is fear of whom China has established.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongluo, Pugu, Uighur, and a dozen other tribes each field tens of thousands of warriors — together they could crush him instantly, yet they dare not move for fear of the man China crowned khan.

sentences.zh: 今以女妻之，彼自恃大國之婿，雜姓誰敢不服！

translations.literal: Now if we give him our daughter in marriage, he will rely on being the great state's son-in-law — which of the mixed tribes will dare not submit!
translations.idiomatic: Give him our daughter, and armed with the status of the great empire's son-in-law, which mixed tribe would dare resist?

sentences.zh: 戎狄人面獸心，一旦微不得意，必反噬為害。

translations.literal: The barbarians have human faces but beast hearts; if once they are slightly dissatisfied, they will surely turn and bite in harm.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians wear human faces but harbor beasts' hearts — give them the slightest grievance and they will lash back.

sentences.zh: 今吾絕其昏，殺其禮，雜姓知我棄之，不日將瓜剖之矣，卿曹第志之。」

translations.literal: Now that I break off the marriage and cancel the rites, when the mixed tribes know I have cast him off, before long they will carve him up like a melon — you all just keep watch."
translations.idiomatic: Break off the marriage and deny him the rite — once the mixed tribes see I have abandoned him, they will carve up his realm within days. Mark my words."

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：孔子稱去食、去兵，不可去信。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang observes: Confucius said one may do without food, one may do without arms, but one cannot do without trust.
translations.idiomatic: Master Guang comments: Confucius declared that one might forgo food or arms, but never trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗審知薛延陀不可妻，則初勿許其昏可也；

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong clearly knew Xueyantuo ought not receive a princess — then at the outset he ought not to have promised the marriage;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong knew full well that Xueyantuo ought not receive an imperial bride — he should never have promised the marriage in the first place.

sentences.zh: 既許之矣，乃復恃強棄信而絕之，雖滅薛延陀，猶可羞也。

translations.literal: once he had promised, yet again relying on strength he abandoned faith and broke it off — even if Xueyantuo were destroyed, it would still be shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Having promised, he then used China's might to break faith — even destroying Xueyantuo would remain a disgrace.

sentences.zh: 王者發言出令，可不慎哉！

translations.literal: When a king speaks and issues commands — can one not be cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler speaks and commands, can he not be more careful!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「蓋蘇文弒其君而專國政，誠不可忍。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yeongaeso murdered his sovereign and monopolized state power — truly unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yeongaeso killed his king and seized national power — this truly cannot be tolerated.

sentences.zh: 以今日兵力，取之不難，但不欲勞百姓，吾欲且使契丹、靺鞨擾之，何如？」

translations.literal: With today's military strength, taking them would not be difficult — but I do not wish to weary the common people. I intend first to have the Khitan and Mohe harass them — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: With our forces today, conquest would be easy — but I do not wish to burden the people. Perhaps we should let the Khitan and Mohe harry them first — what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌曰：「蓋蘇文自知罪大，畏大國之討，必嚴設守備，陛下姑為之隱忍，彼得以自安，必更驕惰，愈肆其惡，然後討之，未晚也。」

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji said: "Yeongaeso knows his guilt is great and fears punishment from the great state — he will surely fortify defenses rigorously. Your Majesty should for now exercise forbearance in concealment, so that he may feel secure; he will surely grow more arrogant and idle and commit greater outrages — then to strike will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji replied, "Yeongaeso knows his crimes are grave and dreads China's wrath — he will fortify his defenses. Your Majesty should temporarily hold your peace and let him feel secure; growing arrogant and reckless, he will commit worse atrocities — then strike, and it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 戊辰，詔以高麗王藏為上柱國、遼東郡王、高麗王，遣使持節冊命。

translations.literal: On wuchen, an edict appointed Goguryeo King Go Jang as Supreme Pillar of State, Prince of Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo, and dispatched an envoy bearing credentials to invest him.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, an edict invested King Go Jang of Goguryeo as Supreme Pillar of State, Prince of Liaodong Commandery, and King of Goguryeo, and sent an envoy with credentials to confer the titles.

sentences.zh: 丙子，徙東萊王泰為順陽王。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Prince of Donglai Li Tai was moved to be Prince of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Prince of Donglai Li Tai was reassigned as Prince of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 初，太子承乾失德，上密謂中書侍郎兼左庶子杜正倫曰：「吾兒足疾乃可耳，但疏遠賢良，狎暱群小，卿可察之。

translations.literal: Previously, when Crown Prince Chengqian's conduct failed, the emperor secretly told Vice Director of the Secretariat and Left Subordinate Du Zhenlun: "My son's foot ailment is tolerable enough, but he keeps the worthy at a distance and dotes on petty men — you may investigate this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Crown Prince Chengqian's conduct went astray, Emperor Taizong confided to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Left Subordinate Du Zhenlun, "My son's lame foot is bearable — but he shuns worthy men and consorts with petty scoundrels. Watch him closely.

sentences.zh: 果不可教示，當來告我。」

translations.literal: If he truly cannot be taught and guided, you must come and tell me."
translations.idiomatic: If he truly cannot be reformed, come and tell me."

sentences.zh: 正倫屢諫，不聽，乃以上語告之。

translations.literal: Du Zhenlun remonstrated repeatedly but was not heeded; he therefore told the crown prince what the emperor had said.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhenlun remonstrated repeatedly without effect, then revealed the emperor's words to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子抗表以聞，上責正倫漏洩，對曰：「臣以此恐之，冀其遷善耳。」

translations.literal: The crown prince submitted a memorial in protest to inform the emperor. The emperor rebuked Du Zhenlun for leaking secrets. He replied: "Your servant used this to frighten him, hoping he would turn toward goodness."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince lodged a formal protest. The emperor rebuked Du Zhenlun for the leak; he replied, "I meant to frighten him into reform."

sentences.zh: 上怒，出正倫為穀州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent Du Zhenlun out as Prefect of Guchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, the emperor banished Du Zhenlun to serve as Prefect of Guchuan.

sentences.zh: 及承乾敗，秋，七月，辛卯，復左遷正倫為交州都督。

translations.literal: When Chengqian fell, in autumn, the seventh month, on xinmao, Du Zhenlun was again demoted to Military Governor of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengqian's downfall, in the seventh month of autumn, on xinmao, Du Zhenlun was demoted again to Military Governor of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 初，魏徵嘗薦正倫及侯君集有宰相材，請以君集為僕射，且曰：「國家安不忘危，不可無大將，諸衛兵馬宜委君集專知。」

translations.literal: Previously Wei Zheng had once recommended that Du Zhenlun and Hou Junji possessed the talent of chancellors; he requested that Hou Junji be made Vice Director, and said: "When the state is secure one must not forget danger — a great general cannot be dispensed with; the horse troops of the various guards ought to be entrusted to Hou Junji's sole charge."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng had once recommended both Du Zhenlun and Hou Junji as chancellor material, proposed Hou Junji for Vice Director, and argued, "In peace one must not forget peril — the realm needs a great general; the guard cavalry should be placed under Hou Junji's sole command."

sentences.zh: 上以君集好夸誕，不用。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Hou Junji fond of boastful exaggeration and did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Hou Junji boastful and unreliable and declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 及正倫以罪黜，君集謀反誅，上始疑征阿黨。

translations.literal: When Du Zhenlun was dismissed for his offense and Hou Junji was executed for plotting rebellion, the emperor began to suspect Wei Zheng of factional favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: After Du Zhenlun's dismissal and Hou Junji's execution for treason, the emperor began to suspect Wei Zheng of factional favoritism.

sentences.zh: 又有言征自錄前後諫辭以示起居郎褚遂良者，上愈不悅，乃罷叔玉尚主，而踣所撰碑。

translations.literal: There was also report that Wei Zheng had copied his remonstrances over the years to show to Diarist Chu Suiliang — the emperor grew still more displeased and canceled the princess's betrothal to Shuyu and toppled the stele Wei Zheng had composed.
translations.idiomatic: Reports also surfaced that Wei Zheng had copied his past memorials to show Diarist Chu Suiliang. The emperor's displeasure deepened: he canceled the princess's betrothal to Wei Zheng's son Shuyu and demolished the memorial stele.

sentences.zh: 初，上謂監修國史房玄齡曰：「前世史官所記，皆不令人主見之，何也？」

translations.literal: Previously the emperor said to Fang Xuanling, Commissioner for Compiling the National History: "The records kept by historians of former ages were never shown to the ruler — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong once asked Fang Xuanling, overseer of the national history, "Why did historians of old never allow emperors to read their records?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「史官不虛美，不隱惡，若人主見之必怒，故不敢獻也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Historians neither add false praise nor conceal evil. If the ruler saw them he would surely grow angry — therefore they did not dare present them."
translations.idiomatic: Fang replied, "Historians neither flatter nor conceal wrongdoing — an emperor who read them would surely rage, so they dared not submit their drafts."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕之為心，異於前世帝王。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "My disposition differs from emperors of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "My intentions differ from those of earlier emperors.

sentences.zh: 欲自觀國史，知前日之惡，為後來之戒，公可撰次以聞。」

translations.literal: I wish to read the national history myself, to know yesterday's wrongs and make a warning for what follows — you may compile and submit it."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to read the national history myself — to learn from past errors and warn future generations. Compile it and present it to me."

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫朱子奢上言：「陛下聖德在躬，舉無過事，史官所述，義歸盡善。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Review Grand Counselor Zhu Zixia submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty's sagely virtue is embodied in your person; in action there is no fault; what the historians record, in principle, turns entirely on perfection.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Counselor Zhu Zixia memorialized, "Your Majesty's sage virtue is manifest; you commit no misdeeds — the historians' accounts must naturally show only perfection.

sentences.zh: 陛下獨覽《起居》，於事無失，若以此法傳示子孫，竊恐曾、玄之後或非上智，飾非護短，史官必不免刑誅。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty alone reads the Diaries of Activity and Repose, in the matter there is no loss — but if this practice is transmitted to posterity, I privately fear that after Zeng and Yan there may not be superlative wisdom; cloaking faults and shielding shortcomings, historians will surely not escape execution.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty alone reading the court diaries does no harm — but if this custom passes to your descendants, I fear that after men like Zeng Shen and Yan Yuan there will be no sage rulers; emperors will hide faults, and historians will face execution.

sentences.zh: 如此，則莫不希風順旨，全身遠害，悠悠千載，何所信乎！

translations.literal: If so, then none will not court the wind and follow the intent, seeking to preserve themselves and avoid harm — across a thousand years, what would there be to trust!
translations.idiomatic: Then every historian will trim truth to please the throne and save his skin — across a thousand years, what record could anyone trust?

sentences.zh: 所以前代不觀，蓋為此也。」

translations.literal: The reason former ages did not permit viewing was largely this."
translations.idiomatic: Former dynasties forbade emperors from reading history largely for this reason."

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the advice.

sentences.zh: 玄齡乃與給事中許敬宗等刪為《高祖》、《今上實錄》；

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling then joined with Attendant Within Xu Jingzong and others in abridging the Veritable Records of Emperor Gaozu and the Veritable Records of the Present Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling then worked with Attendant Within Xu Jingzong and others to edit the Veritable Records of Emperor Gaozu and the Veritable Records of the Present Emperor;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，書成，上之。

translations.literal: On guisi the work was completed and submitted to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the completed work was submitted.

sentences.zh: 上見書六月四日事，語多微隱，謂玄齡曰：「昔周公誅管、蔡以安周，季友鴆叔牙以存魯。

translations.literal: The emperor saw the account of the events of the fourth day of the sixth month — the language largely veiled and hidden — and said to Fang Xuanling: "In olden days the Duke of Zhou executed Guan and Cai to secure Zhou; Jiyou poisoned Shuya to preserve Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the account of the fourth day of the sixth month, the emperor found the language evasive and cryptic. He told Fang Xuanling, "The Duke of Zhou executed Guan and Cai to save Zhou; Jiyou poisoned Shuya to preserve Lu.

sentences.zh: 朕之所以，亦類是耳，史官何諱焉！」

translations.literal: What I did is likewise of that sort — what need for historians to conceal it!"
translations.idiomatic: My actions were of the same kind — why should the historians hide them?"

sentences.zh: 即命削去浮詞，直書其事。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered the ornamental phrases removed and the matter written plainly.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered the flowery language struck out and the events recorded plainly.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚戌，以洛州都督張亮為刑部尚書，參預朝政；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengxu, Zhang Liang, Military Governor of Luozhou, was appointed Minister of Justice and joined in managing court affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengxu, Military Governor of Luozhou Zhang Liang was appointed Minister of Justice and entered the deliberations of state;

sentences.zh: 以左衛大將軍、太子右衛率李大亮為工部尚書。

translations.literal: Left Guard Grand General and Right Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard Li Daliang was appointed Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard Grand General and Right Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard Li Daliang was named Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 大亮身居三職，宿衛兩宮，恭儉忠謹，每宿直，必坐寐達旦。

translations.literal: Li Daliang held three posts at once, standing night guard for both palaces; respectful, frugal, loyal, and careful — whenever he stood night watch, he would sit and doze until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang held three offices simultaneously, standing guard over both palaces — dutiful, frugal, and loyal. On night watch he always sat awake until dawn.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡甚重之，每稱大亮有王陵、周勃之節，可當大位。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling greatly valued him and often praised that Li Daliang possessed the integrity of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo and could fill the highest position.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling held him in high esteem, often declaring that Li Daliang had the steadfast integrity of Wang Ling and Zhou Bo and was fit for the highest office.

sentences.zh: 初，大亮為龐王兵曹，為李密所獲，同輩皆死，賊帥張弼見而釋之，遂與定交。

translations.literal: Previously, when Li Daliang served as Army Assistant to Prince of Pang, he was captured by Li Mi; all his companions were killed, but the bandit chief Zhang Bi saw him and released him — they thereupon formed a firm friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Li Daliang served as army recorder to Prince of Pang, Li Mi captured him. His comrades were all killed, but the rebel leader Zhang Bi saw him and spared his life — from that day they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 及大亮貴，求弼，欲報其德，弼時為將作丞，自匿不言。

translations.literal: When Li Daliang rose to eminence he sought Zhang Bi, wishing to repay his kindness; Zhang Bi then served as Assistant Director of the Directorate of Imperial Construction and hid himself without speaking of it.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Daliang rose to prominence, he searched for Zhang Bi to repay his debt — but Zhang Bi, then a minor official in the Directorate of Imperial Construction, concealed his identity.

sentences.zh: 大亮遇諸途而識之，持弼而泣，多推家貲以遣弼，弼拒不受。

translations.literal: Li Daliang encountered him on the road and recognized him; he seized Zhang Bi and wept, repeatedly pressing family wealth upon him — Zhang Bi refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang recognized Zhang Bi on the road, embraced him in tears, and pressed his family fortune upon him — but Zhang Bi refused every gift.

sentences.zh: 大亮言於上，乞悉以其官爵授弼，上為之擢弼為中郎將。

translations.literal: Li Daliang spoke to the emperor and begged that all his offices and ranks be transferred to Zhang Bi; the emperor thereupon promoted Zhang Bi to Captain of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daliang petitioned the emperor to confer all his titles and offices on Zhang Bi; the emperor promoted Zhang Bi to Captain of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 時人皆賢大亮不負恩，而多弼之不伐也。

translations.literal: Men of the time all praised Li Daliang for not failing in gratitude, and admired Zhang Bi for not boasting.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised Li Daliang for never forgetting a kindness — and admired Zhang Bi equally for never boasting of his own.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚辰，新羅遣使言百濟攻取其國四十餘城，復與高麗連兵，謀絕新羅入朝之路，乞兵救援。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengchen, Silla sent envoys reporting that Baekje had attacked and seized more than forty of its cities, then joined forces with Goguryeo, plotting to cut off Silla's route to court, begging troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengchen, Silla sent envoys reporting that Baekje had attacked and seized more than forty of its cities, then allied with Goguryeo to block Silla's path to the Tang court and begged for military aid.

sentences.zh: 上命司農丞相裡玄獎繼璽書賜高麗曰：「新羅委質國家，朝貢不乏，爾與百濟各宜戢兵；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Minister of Revenue and Chancellor Xiangli Xuanying to carry on the imperial letter and bestow it on Goguryeo, saying: "Silla has submitted to the state and its tribute has never lapsed; you and Baekje should each rein in your troops;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Minister of Revenue and Chancellor Xiangli Xuanying to deliver a further imperial letter to Goguryeo, saying: "Silla has pledged itself to the empire and never failed in tribute; you and Baekje should each cease hostilities;

sentences.zh: 若更攻之，明年發兵擊爾國矣！」

translations.literal: If you attack again, next year I shall send troops to strike your state!"
translations.idiomatic: If you attack again, next year I shall send troops against your kingdom!"

sentences.zh: 癸未，徙承乾於黔州。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Chengqian was relocated to Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Chengqian was exiled to Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲午，徙順陽王泰於均州。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Prince of Shunyang Tai was relocated to Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Prince of Shunyang Li Tai was exiled to Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「父子之情，出於自然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The feeling between father and son arises from nature.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A father's love for his son is natural.

sentences.zh: 朕今與泰生離，亦何心自處！

translations.literal: Now that I part from Tai in life, what state of mind can I keep for myself!
translations.idiomatic: To part from Tai while we both still live — what peace can I find in my own heart!

sentences.zh: 然朕為天下主，但使百姓安寧，私情亦可割耳。」

translations.literal: Yet as sovereign over all under heaven, so long as the common people are at peace, private feeling may also be set aside."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am sovereign of the realm; if the people are secure, private feeling must yield."

sentences.zh: 又以泰所上表示近臣曰：「泰誠為俊才，朕心念之，卿曹所知；

translations.literal: He also showed Tai's memorial to his close officials and said: "Tai is truly a brilliant talent; I keep him in my thoughts, as you all know;
translations.idiomatic: He also showed Tai's memorial to his close ministers and said, "Tai is truly a gifted man, and I hold him in my thoughts, as you know;

sentences.zh: 但以社稷之故，不得不斷之以義，使之居外者，亦所以兩全之耳。」

translations.literal: But for the sake of the altars of state, I had no choice but to decide by principle of right; sending him to live abroad is also a way to preserve us both."
translations.idiomatic: but for the sake of the realm I must judge by duty, not affection; sending him away is also a way to preserve us both."

sentences.zh: 先是，諸州長官或上佐歲首親奉貢物入京師，謂之朝集使，亦謂之考使；

translations.literal: Earlier, the chief officials or senior assistants of the prefectures at the year's start personally brought tribute goods to the capital; they were called envoys for the court assembly, also called envoys for assessment;
translations.idiomatic: Previously, at the year's opening the chief prefectural officials or their senior deputies personally brought tribute to the capital; they were called envoys for the court assembly, or assessment envoys;

sentences.zh: 京師無邸，率僦屋與商賈雜居。

translations.literal: The capital had no lodges for them, and they generally rented dwellings and lived mixed among merchants.
translations.idiomatic: the capital had no guesthouses for them, and they usually rented rooms and lived among merchants.

sentences.zh: 上始命有司為之作邸。

translations.literal: The emperor first ordered the relevant offices to build lodges for them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the appropriate offices to build lodges for them.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，己卯，上禮圜丘。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on jimao, the emperor performed rites at the Circular Mound altar.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on jimao, the emperor sacrificed at the Circular Mound altar.

sentences.zh: 初，上與隱太子、巢剌王有隙，密明公贈司空封德彝陰持兩端。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor and the Hidden Crown Prince and Prince Chaoci had been estranged, Feng Deyi, Duke of Miming and posthumously Minister of Works, secretly played both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor and the Hidden Crown Prince and Prince Chaoci were at odds, Feng Deyi, Duke of Miming and posthumously Minister of Works, secretly straddled both camps.

sentences.zh: 楊文幹之亂，上皇欲廢隱太子而立上，德彝固諫而止。

translations.literal: During the Yang Wengan revolt, the Retired Emperor wished to depose the Hidden Crown Prince and set up the emperor instead; Deyi remonstrated firmly and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yang Wengan rebellion, the Retired Emperor wished to depose the Hidden Crown Prince and install the emperor in his place; Deyi remonstrated forcefully and halted the plan.

sentences.zh: 其事甚秘，上不之知，薨後乃知之。

translations.literal: The matter was highly secret; the emperor did not know of it until after Deyi's death.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was kept deeply secret; the emperor learned of it only after Deyi's death.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，治書侍御史唐臨始追劾其事，請黜官奪爵。

translations.literal: On renchen, Supervising Secretary Tang Lin first pursued impeachment over the affair and requested dismissal from office and confiscation of rank.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Supervising Secretary Tang Lin first brought charges over the affair and requested that Deyi's offices and titles be stripped.

sentences.zh: 上命百官議之，尚書唐儉等議：「德彝罪暴身後，恩結生前，所歷眾官，不可追奪，請降贈改謚。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the officials to discuss it. Minister Tang Jian and others argued: "Deyi's crime was revealed after his death, but his grace was bound up in his lifetime; the many offices he held cannot be stripped retroactively; we ask that his posthumous gifts be reduced and his posthumous title changed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the officials to deliberate. Minister of Works Tang Jian and others argued: "Deyi's guilt came to light only after his death, yet the honors he earned in life remain; the offices he held cannot all be revoked retroactively — we ask that his posthumous appointments be reduced and his posthumous epithet changed."

sentences.zh: 詔黜其贈官，改謚曰繆，削所食實封。

translations.literal: An edict removed his posthumous appointments, changed his posthumous epithet to Miu, and stripped his substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed his posthumous offices, changed his posthumous epithet to Miu ("Erroneous"), and confiscated his substantive fief.

sentences.zh: 敕選良家女以實東宮；

translations.literal: An edict ordered selecting daughters of good families to fill the Eastern Palace;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that daughters of respectable families be selected to fill the Eastern Palace;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，太子遣左庶子於志寧辭之。

translations.literal: On guisi, the Crown Prince sent Left Supervisor of the Heir Apparent Yu Zhining to decline.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, the Crown Prince sent Left Supervisor Yu Zhining to decline the offer.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吾不欲使子孫生於微賤耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I merely do not want my descendants born of humble stock.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I only meant to keep my descendants from being born to humble stock.

sentences.zh: 今既致辭，當從其意。」

translations.literal: Now that you have formally declined, I shall follow your wish."
translations.idiomatic: Since you have formally declined, I shall respect your wish."

sentences.zh: 上疑太子仁弱，密謂長孫無忌曰：「公勸我立雉權，雉奴懦，恐不能守社稷，奈何！

translations.literal: The emperor suspected the Crown Prince was gentle and weak. He told Zhangsun Wuji in secret: "You urged me to install Zhiquan; Zhiqu is timid — I fear he cannot hold the altars of state. What is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted the Crown Prince was too mild and weak. He told Zhangsun Wuji in secret, "You urged me to install Zhiquan; the boy Zhiqu is timid — I fear he cannot hold the realm. What can be done?

sentences.zh: 吳王恪英果類我，我欲立之，何如？」

translations.literal: Prince of Wu Ke is bold and resolute like me — I wish to install him. What do you think?"
