translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wu Li Ke is bold and resolute like me; I wish to make him heir. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 無忌固爭，以為不可。

translations.literal: Wuji argued strenuously that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji argued strenuously that it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「公以恪非己之甥邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Do you think Ke is not your nephew?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Do you think Ke is not your own nephew?"

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「太子仁厚，真守文良主；

translations.literal: Wuji said: "The Crown Prince is humane and generous — truly a fine ruler who would maintain the established order;
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said, "The Crown Prince is humane and generous — truly a ruler who would preserve the established order;

sentences.zh: 儲副至重，豈可數易？

translations.literal: The heir apparent is far too important — how can he be changed repeatedly?
translations.idiomatic: the heir apparent is far too weighty a matter — how can he be changed again and again?

sentences.zh: 願陛下熟思之。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to consider this carefully."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh this carefully."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬子，上謂吳王恪曰：「父子雖至親，及其有罪，則天下之法不可私也。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renzi, the emperor told Prince of Wu Ke: "Though father and son are closest of kin, when guilt is involved the laws of all under heaven cannot be bent by private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renzi, the emperor told Prince of Wu Li Ke, "Though father and son are closest of kin, when guilt is involved the laws of the realm cannot be bent for private feeling.

sentences.zh: 漢已立昭帝，燕王旦不服，陰圖不軌，霍光折簡誅之。

translations.literal: When Han had set up Emperor Zhao, Prince of Yan Dan refused to submit, secretly plotted treason, and Huo Guang broke a letter and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Han had enthroned Emperor Zhao, Prince of Yan Dan refused to submit, secretly plotted rebellion, and Huo Guang broke a letter and had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 為人臣子，不可不戒！」

translations.literal: As ministers and sons — none may fail to take warning!"
translations.idiomatic: As subjects and sons, you must take warning from this!"

sentences.zh: 庚申，車賀幸驪山溫湯；

translations.literal: On gengshen, the imperial carriage visited the hot springs at Mount Li;
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the emperor visited the hot springs at Mount Li;

sentences.zh: 庚午，還宮。

translations.literal: On gengwu, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙未，車駕幸鐘官城；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yiwei, the imperial carriage visited Zhongguan City;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yiwei, the emperor visited Zhongguan City;

sentences.zh: 庚子，幸鄠縣；

translations.literal: On gengzi, he visited Hu County;
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, he visited Hu County;

sentences.zh: 壬寅，幸驪山溫湯。

translations.literal: On renyin, he visited the hot springs at Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, he visited the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 相裡玄獎至平壤，莫離支已將兵擊新羅，破其兩城，高麗王使召之，乃還。

translations.literal: Xiangli Xuanying reached Pyongyang; Molizhi had already led troops against Silla and captured two of its cities; the King of Goguryeo sent to summon him, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangli Xuanying reached Pyongyang. Molizhi had already led troops against Silla and taken two of its cities; the King of Goguryeo summoned him back, and he returned.

sentences.zh: 玄獎諭使勿攻新羅，莫離支曰：「昔隋人入寇，新羅乘釁侵我地五百里，自非歸我侵地，恐兵未能已。」

translations.literal: Xuanying instructed him not to attack Silla. Molizhi said: "In the past when Sui invaders came, Silla seized the opportunity to encroach on our territory for five hundred li; unless our seized lands are returned, I fear the fighting cannot cease."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanying urged him not to attack Silla. Molizhi said, "When Sui invaders came in the past, Silla seized the chance to encroach on our territory for five hundred li; unless those lands are returned, I fear the fighting will not stop.

sentences.zh: 玄獎曰：「既往之事，焉可追論！

translations.literal: Xuanying said: "What is past — how can it be argued over again!
translations.idiomatic: Xuanying said, "What is past cannot be argued over again!

sentences.zh: 至於遼東諸城，本皆中國郡縣，中國尚且不言，高麗豈得必求故地！」

translations.literal: As for the cities of Liaodong, they were originally all commanderies and counties of China; even China does not press the claim — how can Goguryeo insist on recovering old territory!"
translations.idiomatic: As for the cities of Liaodong, they were originally commanderies and counties of China; even China does not press the claim — how can Goguryeo insist on recovering old territory!"

sentences.zh: 莫離支竟不從。

translations.literal: Molizhi in the end did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Molizhi refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙巳朔，玄獎還，且言其狀。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day (yisi), Xuanying returned and reported the situation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day (yisi), Xuanying returned and reported what had happened.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「蓋蘇文弒其君，賊其大臣，殘虐其民，今又違我詔命，侵暴鄰國，不可以不討。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Gaesomun murdered his lord, killed his great ministers, and cruelly oppressed his people; now he again defies my edict and violently encroaches on a neighboring state — he cannot go unpunished."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Gaesomun murdered his king, slaughtered his ministers, and cruelly oppressed his people; now he defies my edict and attacks a neighboring state — he must be punished."

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫褚遂良曰：「陛下指麾則中原清晏，顧眄則四夷讋服，威望大矣。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Policy Adviser Chu Suiliang said: "When Your Majesty commands, the Central Plains are calm and quiet; at a glance the four barbarians submit in fear — your authority is already great.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and Policy Adviser Chu Suiliang said, "When Your Majesty commands, the Central Plains are tranquil; at a glance the four quarters submit in awe — your prestige is already immense.

sentences.zh: 今乃渡海遠征小夷，若指期克捷，猶可也。

translations.literal: To cross the sea now on a distant campaign against a petty tribe — if victory comes within the appointed time, it may still be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: To cross the sea now on a distant expedition against a petty state — if victory comes within the appointed time, that may still be acceptable.

sentences.zh: 萬一蹉跌，傷威損望，更興忿兵，則安危難測矣。」

translations.literal: But if you stumble even once, prestige will be wounded and hopes diminished; if angry troops are raised again, then safety and peril become impossible to foretell."
translations.idiomatic: But if you stumble even once, prestige will be wounded and confidence shaken; if angry troops must be raised again, then safety and peril become impossible to foretell."

sentences.zh: 李世勣曰：「間者薛延陀入寇，陛下欲發兵窮討，魏徵諫而止，使至今為患。

translations.literal: Li Shiji said: "Recently when Xueyantuo invaded, Your Majesty wished to send troops to pursue and destroy them, but Wei Zheng remonstrated and stopped it — leaving them a source of trouble to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji said, "When Xueyantuo invaded not long ago, Your Majesty wished to send troops to pursue and destroy them, but Wei Zheng remonstrated and stopped it — and they have been a menace ever since.

sentences.zh: 向用陛下之策，北鄙安矣。」

translations.literal: Had Your Majesty's plan been followed then, the northern frontier would be secure."
translations.idiomatic: Had Your Majesty's plan been followed then, the northern frontier would be secure today."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "True.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "True.

sentences.zh: 此誠徵之失，朕尋悔之而不欲言，恐塞良謀故也。」

translations.literal: That was indeed Zheng's error; I soon regretted it but did not wish to say so, for fear of blocking good counsel."
translations.idiomatic: That was indeed Zheng's mistake; I soon regretted it but did not say so, for fear of discouraging sound counsel."

sentences.zh: 上欲自征高麗，褚遂良上疏，以為：「天下譬猶一身：兩京，心腹也；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to campaign against Goguryeo in person. Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial arguing: "The realm is like a single body: the Two Capitals are the heart and viscera;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to campaign against Goguryeo in person. Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial arguing that the realm is like a single body: the Two Capitals are its heart and viscera;

sentences.zh: 州縣，四支也；

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties are the four limbs;
translations.idiomatic: the prefectures and counties are its four limbs;

sentences.zh: 四夷，身外之物也。

translations.literal: The four barbarians are things outside the body.
translations.idiomatic: and the four quarters are things outside the body.

sentences.zh: 高麗罪大，誠當致討，但命二、三猛將將四五萬眾，仗陛下威靈，取之如反掌耳。

translations.literal: Goguryeo's crime is grave and truly calls for punishment; but if two or three fierce generals are sent with forty or fifty thousand men, relying on Your Majesty's august power, taking it would be like turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo's crimes are grave and truly call for punishment, but send two or three fierce generals with forty or fifty thousand men, and relying on Your Majesty's august power you will take it as easily as turning your palm.

sentences.zh: 今太子新立，年尚幼稚，自餘籓屏，陛下所知，一旦棄金湯之全，逾遼海之險，以天下之君，輕行遠舉，皆愚臣之所甚憂也。」

translations.literal: Now the Crown Prince has just been installed and is still young; the rest of the feudatory bulwarks are as Your Majesty knows — to abandon impregnable security at a stroke, cross the peril of the Liaohai Sea, and as sovereign of all under heaven undertake a light-handed distant expedition — this is what your foolish minister most dreads."
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince has just been installed and is still young; the rest of the feudatory bulwarks are as Your Majesty knows. To abandon impregnable security at a stroke, cross the peril of the Liaohai Sea, and as sovereign of all under heaven undertake a distant campaign on a whim — this is what your foolish minister most dreads."

sentences.zh: 上不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時群臣多諫征高麗者，上曰：「八堯、九舜，不能冬種，野夫、童子，春種而生，得時故也。

translations.literal: At the time many ministers remonstrated against campaigning against Goguryeo. The emperor said: "Eight Yaos and nine Shuns could not sow in winter; a field hand or a child sows in spring and the crop lives — because the season is right.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many ministers remonstrated against the Goguryeo campaign. The emperor said, "Eight Yaos and nine Shuns could not sow in winter; a field hand or a child sows in spring and the crop lives — because the season is right.

sentences.zh: 夫天有其時，人有其功。

translations.literal: Heaven has its seasons; men have their accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has its seasons; men have their moment to act.

sentences.zh: 蓋蘇文陵上虐下，民延頸待救，此正高麗可亡之時也。

translations.literal: Gaesomun insults those above and brutalizes those below; the people stretch their necks awaiting rescue — this is precisely the hour when Goguryeo may perish.
translations.idiomatic: Gaesomun insults his superiors and brutalizes his people; the folk stretch their necks awaiting rescue — this is precisely the hour when Goguryeo may perish.

sentences.zh: 議者紛紜，但不見此耳。」

translations.literal: The debaters clamor in confusion but do not see this."
translations.idiomatic: The debaters clamor in confusion but fail to see this."

sentences.zh: 己酉，上幸靈口；

translations.literal: On jiyou, the emperor visited Lingkou;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, the emperor visited Lingkou;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，還宮。

translations.literal: On yimao, he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛卯，以左衛將軍薛萬徹守石衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinmao, Left Guard General Xue Wanche was made Defender-General of the Stone Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinmao, Left Guard General Xue Wanche was appointed Defender-General of the Stone Guard.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂侍臣曰：「於今名將，惟世勣、道宗、萬徹三人而已，世勣、道宗不能大勝，亦不大敗，萬徹非大勝則大敗。」

translations.literal: The emperor once told his attendants: "Among famous generals today, only Shiji, Daozong, and Wanche remain. Shiji and Daozong cannot score great victories, but neither do they suffer great defeats; with Wanche it is great victory or great defeat — nothing between."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told his attendants, "Among famous generals today, only Shiji, Daozong, and Wanche remain. Shiji and Daozong neither win great victories nor suffer great defeats; with Wanche it is great victory or great defeat — nothing in between."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，上御兩儀殿，皇太子侍。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the emperor held court in the Hall of Two Principles; the Crown Prince attended.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the emperor held court in the Hall of Two Principles with the Crown Prince in attendance.

sentences.zh: 上謂群臣曰：「太子性行，外人亦聞之乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the ministers: "Has the Crown Prince's character and conduct reached those outside as well?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the ministers, "Has word of the Crown Prince's character and conduct reached those outside the palace?"

sentences.zh: 司徒無忌曰：「太子雖不出宮門，天下無不欽仰聖德。」

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wuji said: "Though the Crown Prince never leaves the palace gates, none under heaven fails to admire his sagely virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhangsun Wuji said, "Though the Crown Prince never leaves the palace gates, none under heaven fails to admire his sagely virtue."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吾如治年時，頗不能御常度。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When I was Zhi's age, I could hardly keep within ordinary bounds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When I was Zhi's age, I could hardly keep within ordinary bounds.

sentences.zh: 治自幼寬厚，諺曰：『生子如狼，猶恐如羊。』

translations.literal: Zhi has been broad and generous from childhood. A proverb says: 'Bear a son like a wolf — yet fear he will prove a sheep.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhi has been mild and generous from childhood. A proverb says, 'Bear a son like a wolf — yet fear he will prove a sheep.'

sentences.zh: 冀其稍壯，自不同耳。」

translations.literal: I hope that as he grows stronger he will prove different."
translations.idiomatic: I hope that as he grows stronger he will prove different."

sentences.zh: 無忌對曰：「陛下神武，乃撥亂之才，太子仁恕，實守文之德；

translations.literal: Wuji replied: "Your Majesty is divinely martial — a talent for quelling chaos; the Crown Prince is humane and forgiving — truly the virtue of keeping the peace;
translations.idiomatic: Wuji replied, "Your Majesty is divinely martial — a talent for quelling chaos; the Crown Prince is humane and forgiving — truly the virtue of preserving peace;

sentences.zh: 趣尚雖異，各當其分，此乃皇天所以祚大唐而福蒼生者也。

translations.literal: Their inclinations differ, yet each suits his role — this is how Heaven blesses Great Tang and brings fortune to the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: their inclinations differ, yet each suits his role — this is how Heaven blesses Great Tang and brings fortune to the people.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，上幸九成宮。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 壬子，至太平宮，謂侍臣曰：「人臣順旨者多，犯顏則少，今朕欲自聞其失，諸公其直言無隱。」

translations.literal: On renzi, he reached Taiping Palace and told his attendants: "Among ministers, many conform to my wishes; few risk my displeasure. Now I wish to hear my own faults myself — speak frankly, with nothing held back."
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, he reached Taiping Palace and told his attendants, "Ministers who agree with me are many; those who risk my displeasure are few. Now I wish to hear my own faults — speak frankly and hold nothing back.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌等皆曰：「陛下無失。」

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji and the rest all said: "Your Majesty has no faults."
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji and the rest all said, "Your Majesty has no faults."

sentences.zh: 劉洎曰：「頃有上書不稱旨者，陛下皆面加窮詰，無不慚懼而退，恐非所以廣言路。

translations.literal: Liu Ji said: "Recently when memorials have not suited Your Majesty's intent, you have questioned the authors to their faces until all withdrew in shame and fear — I fear this is not how to broaden the channels of speech.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji said, "When memorials lately have not suited Your Majesty's intent, you have questioned the authors to their faces until all withdrew in shame and fear — I fear this is not how to broaden the channels of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 馬周曰：「陛下比來賞罰，微以喜怒有所高下，此外不見其失。」

translations.literal: Ma Zhou said: "Your Majesty's rewards and punishments lately have risen or fallen slightly with pleasure and anger; beyond that I see no fault."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou said, "Your Majesty's rewards and punishments lately have risen or fallen slightly with pleasure and anger; beyond that I see no fault."

sentences.zh: 上皆納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted all of it.

sentences.zh: 上好文學而辯敏，群臣言事者，上引古今以折之，多不能對。

translations.literal: The emperor loved literature and was quick in debate; when ministers spoke on affairs of state, he would cite antiquity and the present to refute them, and most could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved literature and was quick in debate; when ministers spoke on affairs of state, he would cite antiquity and the present to refute them, and most could not answer.

sentences.zh: 劉洎上書諫曰：「帝王之與凡庶，聖哲之與庸愚，上下相懸，擬倫斯絕。

translations.literal: Liu Ji submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Between emperor and commoner, sage and fool, above and below are worlds apart — comparison itself breaks down.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Between emperor and commoner, sage and fool, the gulf between high and low is absolute — comparison itself breaks down.

sentences.zh: 是知以至愚而對至聖，以極卑而對至尊，徒思自強，不可得也。

translations.literal: To know that the utterly foolish must answer the utterly sage, the utterly low must answer the utterly exalted — to think one can strengthen oneself thus is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: When the utterly foolish must answer the utterly sage, and the utterly low must answer the utterly exalted, to think one can strengthen oneself by debate is impossible.

sentences.zh: 陛下降恩旨，假慈顏，凝旒以聽其言，虛襟以納其說，猶恐群下未敢對揚；

translations.literal: Your Majesty lowers gracious edicts, lends a kindly countenance, focuses beneath the hanging tassels to hear their words, opens an empty breast to receive their views — yet still fears those below may not dare respond openly;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty lowers gracious edicts, lends a kindly countenance, listens beneath the hanging tassels, and opens your breast to receive their views — yet still fears those below may not dare respond openly;

sentences.zh: 況動神機，縱天辯，飾辭以折其理，引古以排其議，欲令凡庶何階應答！

translations.literal: How much less when you deploy divine ingenuity, unleash heaven's eloquence, dress up arguments to break their reasoning, cite antiquity to crush their proposals — and expect commoners to find any footing to reply!
translations.idiomatic: how much less when you deploy divine ingenuity, unleash heaven's eloquence, dress up arguments to break their reasoning, and cite antiquity to crush their proposals — and expect commoners to find any footing to reply!

sentences.zh: 且多記則損心，多語則損氣，心氣內損，形神外勞，初雖不覺，後必為累。

translations.literal: Moreover, much memorizing harms the heart; much speaking harms the breath. Heart and breath depleted inwardly, body and spirit exhausted outwardly — at first one does not notice, but in time it must become a burden.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, much memorizing harms the heart; much speaking harms the breath. Heart and breath depleted inwardly, body and spirit exhausted outwardly — at first one does not notice, but in time it must become a burden.

sentences.zh: 須為社稷自愛，豈為性好自傷乎！

translations.literal: You must cherish yourself for the altars of state — not indulge a nature that injures its own self!
translations.idiomatic: You must cherish yourself for the sake of the realm — not indulge a nature that injures its own self!

sentences.zh: 至如秦政強辯，失人心於自矜；

translations.literal: Consider Qin Shihuang's fierce disputation — he lost hearts through self-conceit;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Qin Shihuang's fierce disputation — he lost the hearts of men through self-conceit;

sentences.zh: 魏文宏才，虧從望於虛說。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei had vast talent — yet he forfeited followers' respect through empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei had vast talent — yet he forfeited his followers' respect through empty talk.

sentences.zh: 此才辯之累，較然可知矣。」

translations.literal: The burden of brilliance in disputation — how clearly this shows it."
translations.idiomatic: The burden of brilliance in disputation — how clearly this shows it."

sentences.zh: 上飛白答之曰：「非慮無以臨下，非言無以述慮，比有談論，遂致煩多，輕物驕人，恐由茲道，形神心氣，非此為勞。

translations.literal: The emperor answered in flying-white script: "Without thought one cannot oversee those below; without words one cannot express thought. Lately discussions have grown numerous and tedious — slighting things and arrogant toward men, I fear, may stem from this path; body, spirit, heart, and breath are not exhausted by this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered in flying-white script: "Without thought one cannot oversee those below; without words one cannot express thought. Lately discussions have grown numerous and tedious — slighting things and arrogant toward men, I fear, may stem from this path; body, spirit, heart, and breath are not exhausted by this.

sentences.zh: 今聞讜言，虛懷以改。」

translations.literal: Now hearing honest counsel, I open my heart to amend.
translations.idiomatic: Now hearing honest counsel, I open my heart to amend."

sentences.zh: 己未，至顯仁宮。

translations.literal: On jiwei, he arrived at Xianren Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the emperor arrived at Xianren Palace.

sentences.zh: 上將征高麗，秋，七月，辛卯，敕將作大監閻立德等詣洪、饒、江三州，造船四百艘以載軍糧。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to campaign against Goguryeo. In autumn, the seventh month, on xinmao, he ordered the Director of Palace Construction Yan Lide and others to proceed to the three prefectures of Hong, Rao, and Jiang to build four hundred ships to carry army grain.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was preparing to campaign against Goguryeo. In autumn, the seventh month, on xinmao, he ordered Yan Lide, Director of Palace Construction, and others to proceed to Hong, Rao, and Jiang Prefectures to build four hundred ships for transporting army provisions.

sentences.zh: 甲午，下詔遣營州都督張儉等帥幽、營二都督兵及契丹、奚、靺鞨先擊遼東以觀其勢。

translations.literal: On jiawu, an edict was issued dispatching Yingzhou Protector-General Zhang Jian and others to lead the troops of the two protectorates of You and Ying, together with Khitan, Xi, and Mohe, to strike Liaodong first and observe the enemy's strength.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, an edict dispatched Zhang Jian, Protector-General of Yingzhou, and others to lead the armies of the You and Ying protectorates, along with Khitan, Xi, and Mohe forces, to strike Liaodong first and test the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 以太常卿韋挺為饋運使，以民部侍郎崔仁師副之，自河北諸州皆受挺節度，聽以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Wei Ting, Minister of Ceremonies, was made Provision-Transport Commissioner, with Cui Renshi, Vice Minister of Revenue, as his deputy; from all prefectures north of the Yellow River onward, all were placed under Ting's command, with authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ting, Minister of Ceremonies, was appointed Provision-Transport Commissioner, with Cui Renshi, Vice Minister of Revenue, as his deputy. All prefectures north of the Yellow River were placed under Ting's command, with authority to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 又命太僕卿蕭銳運河南諸州糧入海。

translations.literal: He also ordered Xiao Rui, Minister of Imperial Stud, to transport grain from the Henan prefectures by sea.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Xiao Rui, Minister of the Imperial Stud, to transport grain from the Henan prefectures by sea.

sentences.zh: 銳，瑀之子也。

translations.literal: Rui was a son of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was a son of Xiao Yu.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬子，上謂司徒無忌等曰：「人若不自知其過，卿可為朕明言之。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renzi, the emperor said to Chamberlain Wuji and the others: "If a man does not know his own faults, you may speak them plainly to me.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renzi, the emperor said to Zhangsun Wuji, Chamberlain of the Realm, and the others: "If one does not know one's own faults, you may speak them plainly to me.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下武功文德，臣等將順之不暇，又何過之可言！」

translations.literal: They replied: "Your Majesty's martial accomplishments and civil virtue — we are hard pressed to follow them, so how could any fault be spoken of!
translations.idiomatic: They replied: "Your Majesty's martial accomplishments and civil virtue leave us hard pressed to keep pace — how could we speak of any fault!

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕問公以己過，公等乃曲相諛悅，朕欲面舉公等得失以相戒而改之，何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I asked you about my faults, yet you craftily flatter and please one another. I wish to set before you each man's strengths and weaknesses face to face, as mutual warning for improvement — what of it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I asked you about my faults, yet you craftily flatter and please me. I wish to set before you each man's strengths and weaknesses face to face, as mutual warning for improvement — what say you?

sentences.zh: 皆拜謝。

translations.literal: All bowed and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: All bowed and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「長孫無忌善避嫌疑，應物敏速，決斷事理，古人不過；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zhangsun Wuji is good at avoiding suspicion, quick in response to events, and decisive in handling affairs — the ancients could not surpass him;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Zhangsun Wuji is skilled at avoiding suspicion, quick in response to events, and decisive in handling affairs — the ancients could not surpass him;

sentences.zh: 而總兵攻戰，非其所長。

translations.literal: yet commanding troops in attack and battle is not his strong suit.
translations.idiomatic: yet commanding troops in attack and battle is not his strong suit.

sentences.zh: 高士廉涉獵古今，心術明達，臨難不改節，當官無朋黨；

translations.literal: Gao Shilian ranges broadly over ancient and modern learning, with clear and penetrating mind; he does not alter his integrity in adversity, and holds office without faction;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shilian ranges broadly over ancient and modern learning, with a clear and penetrating mind; he does not alter his integrity in adversity, and holds office without faction;

sentences.zh: 所乏者骨鯁規諫耳。

translations.literal: What he lacks is bone-in-throat remonstrance, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: What he lacks is frank, bone-in-throat remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 唐儉言辭辯捷，善和解人；

translations.literal: Tang Jian's words are eloquent and quick, and he is good at reconciling people;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian is eloquent and quick of speech, and skilled at reconciling people;

sentences.zh: 事朕三十年，遂無言及於獻替。

translations.literal: Serving me thirty years, yet never a word touching on proposing and replacing.
translations.idiomatic: He has served me thirty years, yet never once offered counsel on proposing and replacing policy.

sentences.zh: 楊師道性行純和，自無愆違；

translations.literal: Yang Shidao's nature and conduct are pure and gentle, with no fault of his own;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shidao's nature and conduct are pure and gentle, without fault of his own;

sentences.zh: 而情實怯懦，緩急不可得力。

translations.literal: Yet his disposition is truly timid and weak — in urgent need he cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his disposition is truly timid and weak — in urgent need he cannot be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 岑文本性質敦厚，文章華贍；

translations.literal: Cen Wenben's character is sincere and generous, his prose brilliant and rich;
translations.idiomatic: Cen Wenben's character is sincere and generous, his prose brilliant and rich;

sentences.zh: 而持論恆據經遠，自當不負於物。

translations.literal: Yet he always anchors argument in distant classics — by nature he cannot fail men's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he always anchors his arguments in distant classics — by nature he cannot fail men's expectations.

sentences.zh: 劉洎性最堅貞，有利益；

translations.literal: Liu Ji's character is most steadfast and resolute, with benefit to affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji's character is most steadfast and resolute, and of benefit to affairs;

sentences.zh: 然其意尚然諾，私於朋友。

translations.literal: Yet his heart still values pledges — he is partial to friends.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his heart still values pledges of friendship — he is partial to his friends.

sentences.zh: 馬周見事敏速，性甚貞正，論量人物，直道而言，朕比任使，多能稱意。

translations.literal: Ma Zhou sees affairs with quick insight, nature very upright; in judging men he speaks the straight path. In my recent assignments, he has mostly met my wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou sees affairs with quick insight and is very upright by nature; in judging men he speaks the straight path. In my recent assignments, he has mostly met my wishes.

sentences.zh: 褚遂良學問稍長，性亦堅正，每寫忠誠，親附於朕，譬如飛鳥依人，人自憐之。」

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang's learning is somewhat deep, his nature likewise firm and upright; he always inscribes loyalty, drawing close to me — like a bird that nests on a person, whom one naturally pities."
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang's learning is somewhat deep, his nature likewise firm and upright; he always inscribes loyalty and draws close to me — like a bird that nests on a person, whom one naturally pities."

sentences.zh: 甲子，上還京師。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the emperor returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以散騎常侍劉洎為侍中，行中書侍郎岑文本為中書令，太子左庶子中書侍郎馬周守中書令。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Liu Ji, Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; Acting Under Secretary of the Secretariat Cen Wenben was made Grand Secretary; and Left Assistant to the Crown Prince and Under Secretary Ma Zhou was appointed acting Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Liu Ji, Attendant Cavalier-in-Ordinary, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; Cen Wenben, Acting Under Secretary of the Secretariat, was made Grand Secretary; and Ma Zhou, Left Assistant to the Crown Prince and Under Secretary of the Secretariat, was appointed acting Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 文本既拜，還家，有憂色。

translations.literal: After Wenben received the appointment, he returned home with a troubled look.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenben received the appointment, he returned home with a troubled look.

sentences.zh: 母問其故，文本曰：「非勳非舊，濫荷寵榮，位高責重，所以憂懼。」

translations.literal: His mother asked why. Wenben said: "Without merit or longstanding service, I have received favor and glory undeserved; the post is high and responsibility heavy — hence my fear and anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: His mother asked why. Wenben said: "Without merit or longstanding service, I have received favor and glory undeserved; the post is high and the responsibility heavy — hence my fear and anxiety.

sentences.zh: 親賓有來賀者，文本曰：「今受吊，不受賀也。」

translations.literal: When relatives and guests came to congratulate, Wenben said: "Today I accept condolences, not congratulations."
translations.idiomatic: When relatives and guests came to congratulate, Wenben said: "Today I accept condolences, not congratulations."

sentences.zh: 文本弟文昭為校書郎，喜賓客，上聞之不悅；

translations.literal: Wenben's younger brother Wenzhao was a Collator; he delighted in guests, and when the emperor heard of it he was displeased;
translations.idiomatic: Wenben's younger brother Wenzhao was a Collator; he delighted in entertaining guests, and when the emperor heard of it he was displeased;

sentences.zh: 嘗從容謂文本曰：「卿弟過爾交結，恐為卿累；

translations.literal: He once said at ease to Wenben: "Your brother associates overmuch — I fear this may be your burden;
translations.idiomatic: He once said at ease to Wenben: "Your brother associates overmuch — I fear this may burden you;

sentences.zh: 朕欲出為外官，何如？」

translations.literal: I wish to send him out as an official in the provinces — what say you?
translations.idiomatic: I wish to send him out as a provincial official — what say you?

sentences.zh: 文本泣曰：「臣弟少孤，老母特所鍾愛，未嘗信宿離左右。

translations.literal: Wenben wept and said: "My brother was orphaned young; our old mother especially dotes on him — never has he spent a night away from her side.
translations.idiomatic: Wenben wept and said: "My brother was orphaned young; our old mother especially dotes on him — never has he spent a night away from her side.

sentences.zh: 今若出外，母必愁悴，倘無元此弟，亦無老母矣。」

translations.literal: If he goes out now, mother will surely fall into grief and wasting; if not for this younger brother, there would be no old mother either.
translations.idiomatic: If he goes out now, mother will surely fall into grief and wasting; if not for this younger brother, there would be no old mother either.

sentences.zh: 因歔欷嗚咽。

translations.literal: And he sobbed and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: And he sobbed and wailed.

sentences.zh: 上愍其意而止，惟召文昭嚴戒之，亦卒無過。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied his meaning and desisted; he only summoned Wenzhao and sternly warned him, and in the end there was no fault.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pitied his plea and desisted; he only summoned Wenzhao and sternly warned him, and in the end there was no further trouble.

sentences.zh: 九月，以諫議大夫褚遂良為黃門侍郎，參預朝政。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Remonstrance Adviser Chu Suiliang was made Deputy Director of the Chancellery, participating in court governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Chu Suiliang, Remonstrance Adviser, was made Deputy Director of the Chancellery, with a role in court governance.

sentences.zh: 焉耆貳於西突厥，西突厥大臣屈利啜為其弟娶焉耆王女，由是朝貢多闕；

translations.literal: Karasahr turned disloyal to the Western Turks; the Western Turk minister Qulichuo had his younger brother marry the Karasahr king's daughter, and thus tribute missions were often absent;
translations.idiomatic: Karasahr turned disloyal to the Western Turks; the Western Turk minister Qulichuo had his younger brother marry the Karasahr king's daughter, and thus tribute missions were often absent;

sentences.zh: 安西都護郭孝恪請討之。

translations.literal: Protector-General of Anxi Guo Xiaoge requested to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiaoge, Protector-General of Anxi, requested permission to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 詔以孝恪為西州道行軍總管，帥步騎三千出銀山道以擊之。

translations.literal: An edict made Xiaoge Marshal on the Xizhou Route, leading three thousand infantry and cavalry out via the Yinshan Route to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xiaoge Marshal on the Xizhou Route, leading three thousand infantry and cavalry out via the Yinshan Route to strike them.

sentences.zh: 全焉耆王弟頡鼻兄弟三人至西州，孝恪以頡鼻弟栗婆准為鄉導。

translations.literal: The three brothers, including the Karasahr king's younger brother Pinbi, reached Xizhou in full; Xiaoge used Pinbi's brother Lipozhun as guide.
translations.idiomatic: The three brothers, including the Karasahr king's younger brother Pinbi, reached Xizhou safely; Xiaoge used Pinbi's brother Lipozhun as guide.

sentences.zh: 焉耆城四面皆水，恃險而不設備，孝恪倍道兼行，夜，至城下，命將士浮水而渡，比曉，登城，執其王突騎支，獲首虜七千級，留栗婆准攝國事而還。

translations.literal: Karasahr city was girt by water on all sides; trusting the terrain, they made no preparations. Xiaoge marched at double speed, and by night reached the walls; he ordered officers and men to float across the water. By daybreak they had scaled the walls, seized King Tuqizhi, took seven thousand enemy heads, left Lipozhun to govern affairs, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Karasahr city was girt by water on all sides; trusting the terrain, they made no preparations. Xiaoge marched at double speed and by night reached the walls; he ordered his officers and men to float across the water. By daybreak they had scaled the walls, seized King Tuqizhi, took seven thousand enemy heads, left Lipozhun to govern affairs, and returned.

sentences.zh: 孝恪去三日，屈利啜引兵救焉耆，不及，執栗婆准，以勁騎五千，追孝恪至銀山，孝恪還擊，破之，追奔數十里。

translations.literal: Three days after Xiaoge departed, Qulichuo led troops to relieve Karasahr but arrived too late; he seized Lipozhun and with five thousand crack cavalry pursued Xiaoge to Yinshan. Xiaoge turned and struck, defeated them, and pursued the rout several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after Xiaoge departed, Qulichuo led troops to relieve Karasahr but arrived too late; he seized Lipozhun and with five thousand crack cavalry pursued Xiaoge to Yinshan. Xiaoge turned and struck, defeated them, and pursued the rout for several tens of li.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上謂侍臣曰：「孝恪近奏稱八月十一日往擊焉耆，二十日應至，必以二十二日破之。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the emperor said to his attendants: "Xiaoge recently reported that on the eleventh day of the eighth month he would set out against Karasahr; on the twentieth he should arrive, and he is certain to break them on the twenty-second.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the emperor said to his attendants: "Xiaoge recently reported that on the eleventh day of the eighth month he would set out against Karasahr; on the twentieth he should arrive, and he is certain to break them on the twenty-second.

sentences.zh: 朕計其道裡，使者今日至矣！」

translations.literal: By my reckoning of the route distance, the messenger should arrive today!
translations.idiomatic: By my reckoning of the route distance, the messenger should arrive today!

sentences.zh: 言未畢，驛騎至。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking, the dispatch rider arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished speaking, the dispatch rider arrived.

sentences.zh: 西突厥處那啜使其吐屯攝焉耆，遣使入貢。

translations.literal: Chunachuo of the Western Turks had his Tukun administer Karasahr and sent envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Chunachuo of the Western Turks had his Tukun administer Karasahr and sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 上數之曰：「我發兵擊得焉耆，汝何人而據之！」

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked them: "I sent troops and captured Karasahr — who are you to occupy it!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked them: "I sent troops and captured Karasahr — who are you to occupy it!

sentences.zh: 吐屯懼，返其國。

translations.literal: Tukun, in fear, returned to his country.
translations.idiomatic: Tukun, in fear, returned to his country.

sentences.zh: 焉耆立栗婆准從父兄薛婆阿那支為王，仍附於處那啜。

translations.literal: Karasahr enthroned Lipozhun's father's younger brother's son Xuepo Anazhi as king, and still attached themselves to Chunachuo.
translations.idiomatic: Karasahr enthroned Lipozhun's cousin Xuepo Anazhi as king and still attached themselves to Chunachuo.

sentences.zh: 乙未，鴻臚奏「高麗莫離支貢白金。」

translations.literal: On yiwei, the Court of State Ceremonial reported: "Moyechu of Goguryeo offers tribute of white gold.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, the Court of State Ceremonial reported: "Moyechu of Goguryeo offers tribute of white gold.

sentences.zh: 褚遂良曰：「莫離支弒其君，九夷所不容，今將討之而納其金，此郜鼎之類也，臣謂不可受。」

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang said: "Moyechu murdered his lord — the nine Yi cannot tolerate him. Now we are about to punish him yet accept his gold — this is the kind of thing as Duke Ding's vessel; I say it must not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang said: "Moyechu murdered his lord — the nine Yi cannot tolerate him. Now we are about to punish him yet accept his gold — this is like Duke Ding's vessel; I say it must not be accepted.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 上謂高麗使者曰：「汝曹皆事高武，有官爵。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the Goguryeo envoys: "You all served King Gao Wu and hold office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the Goguryeo envoys: "You all served King Gao Wu and hold office and rank.

sentences.zh: 莫離支弒逆，汝曹不能復仇，今更為之遊說以欺大國，罪孰大焉！」

translations.literal: Moyechu committed regicide; you could not avenge it, and now you speak on his behalf to deceive the great state — what crime could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: Moyechu committed regicide; you could not avenge it, and now you speak on his behalf to deceive the great state — what crime could be greater!

sentences.zh: 悉以屬大理。

translations.literal: All were handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: All were handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day of the month (xinchou), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day (xinchou), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，車駕行幸洛陽，以房玄齡留守京師，右衛大將軍、工部尚書李大亮副之。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the imperial carriage proceeded to Luoyang. Fang Xuanling was left to guard the capital, with Right Guard General and Minister of Works Li Daliang as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the imperial carriage proceeded to Luoyang. Fang Xuanling was left to guard the capital, with Li Daliang, Right Guard General and Minister of Works, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 郭孝恪鎖焉耆王突騎支及其妻子詣行在，敕宥之。

translations.literal: Guo Xiaoge brought the Karasahr king Tuqizhi and his wife and children in chains to the emperor's presence; an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiaoge brought the Karasahr king Tuqizhi and his wife and children in chains to the emperor's presence; an edict pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，上謂太子曰：「焉耆王不求賢輔，不用忠謀，自取滅亡，繫頸束手，漂搖萬里；

translations.literal: On dingsi, the emperor said to the Crown Prince: "The Karasahr king did not seek worthy aides or use loyal counsel — he brought ruin on himself, bound by the neck with hands tied, adrift ten thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the emperor said to the Crown Prince: "The Karasahr king did not seek worthy aides or heed loyal counsel — he brought ruin on himself, bound by the neck with hands tied, adrift ten thousand li;

sentences.zh: 人以此思懼，則懼可知矣。」

translations.literal: When a man ponders this and feels fear, then how clear fear must be."
translations.idiomatic: When a man ponders this and feels fear, then how clear fear must be."

sentences.zh: 己巳，畋於澠池之天池；

translations.literal: On jisi, he hunted at the Heavenly Pool at Mianchi;
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, he hunted at the Heavenly Pool at Mianchi;

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬申，至洛陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on renshen, he reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renshen, he reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 前宜州刺史鄭元□，已致仕，上以其嘗從隋煬帝伐高麗，召詣行在；

translations.literal: Former Yizhou Prefect Zheng Yuan□, already retired, was summoned to the imperial presence because he had once followed Emperor Yang of Sui in the campaign against Goguryeo;
translations.idiomatic: Former Yizhou Prefect Zheng Yuan□, already retired, was summoned to the imperial presence because he had once followed Emperor Yang of Sui in the campaign against Goguryeo;

sentences.zh: 問之，對曰：「遼東道遠，糧運艱阻；

translations.literal: He questioned him; he replied: "The Liaodong route is distant, and grain transport is difficult and obstructed;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned him; he replied: "The Liaodong route is distant, and grain transport is difficult and obstructed;

sentences.zh: 東夷善守城，攻之不可猝下。」

translations.literal: The Eastern Yi are skilled at holding cities — storming them cannot be done quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Yi are skilled at holding cities — storming them cannot be done quickly.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「今日非隋之比，公但聽之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Today is not comparable to Sui; you need only wait and see."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Today is not comparable to Sui; you need only wait and see."

sentences.zh: 張儉等值遼水漲，久不得濟，上以為畏懦，召儉詣洛陽。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian and the others met the Liao River in flood and for long could not cross. The emperor thought them timid and summoned Jian to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian and the others met the Liao River in flood and for a long time could not cross. The emperor thought them timid and summoned Jian to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 至，具陳山川險易，水草美惡；

translations.literal: On arrival, he fully reported the terrain's dangers and ease, and the quality of water and grass;
translations.idiomatic: On arrival, he fully reported the terrain's dangers and ease, and the quality of water and grass;

sentences.zh: 上悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 上聞洺州刺史程名振善用兵，召問方略，嘉其才敏，勞勉之，曰：「卿有將相之器，朕方將任使。」

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Bozhou Prefect Cheng Mingzhen was skilled in using troops; he summoned him to ask strategy, praised his talent and quickness, encouraged him, and said: "You have the makings of a general and minister — I am just about to employ you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard that Cheng Mingzhen, Prefect of Bozhou, was skilled in using troops; he summoned him to ask strategy, praised his talent and quickness, encouraged him, and said: "You have the makings of a general and minister — I am just about to employ you.

sentences.zh: 名振失不拜謝，上試責怒，以觀其所為，曰：「山東鄙夫，得一刺史，以為富貴極邪！

translations.literal: Mingzhen failed to bow in thanks. The emperor, testing him with rebuke to observe his conduct, said: "Eastern Shandong boor — obtaining one prefecture, do you take that as the pinnacle of wealth and rank!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen failed to bow in thanks. The emperor, testing him with rebuke to observe his conduct, said: "Eastern Shandong boor — obtaining one prefecture, do you take that as the pinnacle of wealth and rank!

sentences.zh: 敢於天子之側，言語粗疏；

translations.literal: You dare, beside the Son of Heaven, to speak coarsely and carelessly;
translations.idiomatic: You dare, beside the Son of Heaven, to speak coarsely and carelessly;

sentences.zh: 又復不拜！」

translations.literal: And again you do not bow!
translations.idiomatic: And again you do not bow!

sentences.zh: 名振謝曰：「疏野之臣，未嘗親奉聖問，適方心思所對，故忘拜耳。」

translations.literal: Mingzhen apologized: "A rustic subject who has never received the sage's questioning in person — just then my mind was on my reply, so I forgot to bow.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen apologized: "A rustic subject who has never received the sage's questioning in person — just then my mind was on my reply, so I forgot to bow.

sentences.zh: 舉止自若，應對愈明辯。

translations.literal: His bearing was unperturbed, and his answers grew clearer and sharper.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was unperturbed, and his answers grew clearer and sharper.

sentences.zh: 上乃歎曰：「房玄齡處朕左右二十餘年，每見朕譴責餘人，顏色無主。

translations.literal: The emperor then sighed and said: "Fang Xuanling has been at my side twenty-odd years; whenever he sees me reprimand others, his face loses all composure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sighed and said: "Fang Xuanling has been at my side twenty-odd years; whenever he sees me reprimand others, his face loses all composure.

sentences.zh: 名振平生未嘗見朕，朕一旦責之，曾無震懾，辭理不失，真奇士也！」

translations.literal: Mingzhen in all his life has never seen me; I rebuked him at once, and he was not shaken in the least — his words and reasoning never failed. A true extraordinary man!
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhen in all his life has never seen me; I rebuked him at once, and he was not shaken in the least — his words and reasoning never failed. A true extraordinary man!

sentences.zh: 即日拜右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed General of the Right Xiaoqi Guard.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was appointed General of the Right Xiaoqi Guard.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以刑部尚書張亮為平壤道行軍大總管，帥江、淮、嶺、硤兵四萬，長安、洛陽募士三千，戰艦五百艘，自萊州泛海趨平壤；

translations.literal: On jiawu, Minister of Justice Zhang Liang was made Grand Marshal of the Pingrang Route, leading forty thousand troops from Jiang, Huai, Ling, and Xia circuits, three thousand men recruited from Chang'an and Luoyang, and five hundred warships — to sail from Laizhou by sea toward Pingrang;
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Zhang Liang, Minister of Justice, was made Grand Marshal of the Pingrang Route, leading forty thousand troops from the Jiang, Huai, Ling, and Xia circuits, three thousand men recruited from Chang'an and Luoyang, and five hundred warships — to sail from Laizhou by sea toward Pingrang;

sentences.zh: 又以太子詹事、左衛率李世勣為遼東道行軍大總管，帥步騎六萬及蘭、河二州降胡趣遼東，兩軍合勢並進。

translations.literal: Li Shiji, Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and Left Guard Commandant, was made Grand Marshal of the Liaodong Route, leading sixty thousand infantry and cavalry plus surrendered barbarians of Lan and He Prefectures toward Liaodong; the two armies were to combine strength and advance together.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji, Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince and Left Guard Commandant, was made Grand Marshal of the Liaodong Route, leading sixty thousand infantry and cavalry plus surrendered barbarians of Lan and He Prefectures toward Liaodong; the two armies were to combine strength and advance together.

sentences.zh: 庚子，諸軍大集於幽州，遣行軍總管姜行本、少府少監丘行淹先督眾工造梯沖於安蘿山。

translations.literal: On gengzi, all armies mustered in great numbers at Youzhou. Marshals Jiang Hangben and Vice Director of the Palace Workshop Qiu Xingyan were first dispatched to oversee the craftsmen building scaling ladders and ram-towers on Mount Anluo.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, all armies mustered in great numbers at Youzhou. Marshals Jiang Hangben and Qiu Xingyan, Vice Director of the Palace Workshop, were first dispatched to oversee the craftsmen building scaling ladders and ram-towers on Mount Anluo.

sentences.zh: 時遠近勇士應募及獻攻城器械者不可勝數，上皆親加損益，取其便易。

translations.literal: At that time warriors near and far who answered the call and those who offered siege engines were beyond counting; the emperor personally revised each design for the better, taking what was convenient and effective.
translations.idiomatic: At that time warriors near and far who answered the call and those who offered siege engines were beyond counting; the emperor personally revised each design for the better, taking what was convenient and effective.

sentences.zh: 又手詔諭天下，以「高麗蓋蘇文弒主虐民，情何可忍！

translations.literal: He also wrote an imperial edict by his own hand to instruct the realm: "Goguryeo's Yeon Gaesomun murdered his lord and tyrannized the people — how can feeling endure this!
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote an imperial edict by his own hand to instruct the realm: "Goguryeo's Yeon Gaesomun murdered his lord and tyrannized the people — how can such cruelty be endured!

sentences.zh: 今欲巡幸幽、薊，問罪遼、碣，所過營頓，無為勞費。」

translations.literal: Now I wish to tour You and Ji, to demand justice at Liao and Jie; wherever I pass, garrison halts must not burden or waste resources.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to tour You and Ji, to demand justice at Liao and Jie; wherever I pass, garrison halts must not burden or waste resources.

sentences.zh: 且言：「昔隋煬帝殘暴其下，高麗王仁愛其民，以思亂之軍擊安和之眾，故不能成功。

translations.literal: And he said: "Formerly Emperor Yang of Sui was brutal to his subjects, while the Goguryeo king loved and cared for his people; with a mutinous army he struck a settled populace — therefore success was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: And he said: "Formerly Emperor Yang of Sui was brutal to his subjects, while the Goguryeo king loved and cared for his people; with a mutinous army he struck a settled populace — therefore success was impossible.

sentences.zh: 今略言必勝之道有五：一曰以大擊小，二曰以順討逆，三曰以治乘亂，四曰以逸敵勞，五曰以悅當怨，何憂不克！

translations.literal: Now, briefly, five paths to certain victory: first, strike the small with the great; second, punish the rebel with the lawful; third, ride order over chaos; fourth, pit rested troops against the weary; fifth, meet resentment with satisfaction — why worry of failure!
translations.idiomatic: Now, briefly, five paths to certain victory: first, strike the small with the great; second, punish the rebel with the lawful; third, ride order over chaos; fourth, pit rested troops against the weary; fifth, meet resentment with satisfaction — why worry of failure!

sentences.zh: 佈告元元，勿為疑懼！」

translations.literal: Proclaim this to all the people — do not doubt or fear!
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim this to all the people — do not doubt or fear!

sentences.zh: 於是凡頓捨供費之縣，減者太半。

translations.literal: Thereupon, of all counties burdened with halt provisions, more than half had their levies reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, of all counties burdened with halt provisions, more than half had their levies reduced.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛丑，武陽懿公李大亮卒於長安，遺表請罷高麗之師。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on xinchou, Li Daliang, Duke of Wuyang, died at Chang'an; his final memorial requested that the Goguryeo campaign be halted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinchou, Li Daliang, Duke of Wuyang, died at Chang'an; his final memorial requested that the Goguryeo campaign be halted.

sentences.zh: 家餘米五斛，布三十匹。

translations.literal: The household had remaining five hu of grain and thirty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The household had remaining five hu of grain and thirty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 親戚早孤為大亮所養，喪之如父者十有五人。

translations.literal: Of relatives orphaned early whom Daliang had raised, fifteen mourned him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Of relatives orphaned early whom Daliang had raised, fifteen mourned him as a father.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，故太子承乾卒於黔州，上為之廢朝，葬以國公禮。

translations.literal: On renyin, the former Crown Prince Chengqian died at Qianzhou. The emperor suspended court for him and buried him with the rites of a state duke.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, the former Crown Prince Chengqian died at Qianzhou. The emperor suspended court for him and buried him with the rites of a state duke.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，詔諸軍及新羅、百濟、奚、契丹分道擊高麗。

translations.literal: On jiayin, an edict ordered all armies, together with Silla, Baekje, the Xi, and the Khitan, to strike Goguryeo by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, an edict ordered all armies, together with Silla, Baekje, the Xi, and the Khitan, to strike Goguryeo by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 初，上遣突厥俟利苾可汗北渡河，薛延陀真珠可汗恐其部落翻動，意甚惡之，豫蓄輕騎於漠北，欲擊之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had sent the Türk Qilibi Khagan north across the river. The Xueyantuo True-Pearl Khagan feared his tribes would shift allegiance and hated the move deeply; he pre-stationed light cavalry north of the desert, intending to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor had sent the Türk Qilibi Khagan north across the river. The Xueyantuo True-Pearl Khagan feared his tribes would shift allegiance and hated the move deeply; he pre-stationed light cavalry north of the desert, intending to strike.

sentences.zh: 上遣使戒敕無得相攻。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys with stern warnings that they must not attack each other.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys with stern warnings that they must not attack each other.

sentences.zh: 真珠可汗對曰：「至尊有命，安敢不從！

translations.literal: Zhenzhu Khan replied: "The Supreme One has given an order — how would I dare not obey!
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhu Khan replied, "When the Son of Heaven commands, how could I dare refuse!

sentences.zh: 然突厥翻覆難期，當其未破之時，歲犯中國，殺人以千萬計。

translations.literal: Yet the Turks are fickle and hard to predict; before they were broken, year after year they violated China, killing people counted in the tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Turks are treacherous and unreliable. Before they were shattered, they raided China year after year, slaying people by the millions.

sentences.zh: 臣以為至尊克之，當剪為奴婢，以賜中國之人；

translations.literal: Your subject thinks that when the Supreme One conquered them, he ought to have cut them down into male and female slaves and given them to the people of China;
translations.idiomatic: In my view, when Your Majesty conquered them, you should have cut them down and made them bondmen and maidservants for the people of China—

sentences.zh: 乃反養之如子，其恩德至矣，而結社率竟反。

translations.literal: yet instead you raised them as sons — your gracious virtue reached its utmost — and Jiesheshuai ultimately rebelled all the same.
translations.idiomatic: —yet instead you nurtured them as though they were your own sons. Your kindness could scarcely have been greater, and still Jiesheshuai rebelled in the end.

sentences.zh: 此屬獸心，安可以人理待也！

translations.literal: This sort have the hearts of beasts — how can one treat them with human reason!
translations.idiomatic: Such people have the hearts of beasts. How can you treat them by human standards!

sentences.zh: 臣荷恩深厚，請為至尊誅之。」

translations.literal: Your subject has received deep grace; I beg to execute them on the Supreme One's behalf."
translations.idiomatic: I have received Your Majesty's deep favor; allow me to put them to death for you."

sentences.zh: 自是數相攻。

translations.literal: From then on they repeatedly attacked each other.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the two sides repeatedly clashed.

sentences.zh: 俟利苾之北渡也，有眾十萬，勝兵四萬人，俟利苾不能撫御，眾不愜服。

translations.literal: When Qilibi crossed north of the river, he had a host of one hundred thousand and forty thousand effectives; Qilibi could not soothe and control them, and the masses were not satisfied and submissive.
translations.idiomatic: When Qilibi led his people north across the river, his following numbered one hundred thousand, including forty thousand fighting men. He could not command them effectively, and the tribes were restless and discontent.

sentences.zh: 戊午，悉棄俟利苾南渡河，請處於勝、夏之間；

translations.literal: On wuwu, all abandoned Qilibi, crossed the river south, and requested to be settled between Sheng and Xia;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the entire tribe deserted Qilibi, crossed the Yellow River to the south, and asked to be resettled between Shengzhou and Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted their request.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆以為：「陛下方遠征遼左，而置突厥於河南，距京師不遠，豈得不為後慮！

translations.literal: All the ministers were of the view: "Your Majesty is about to campaign far to the east in Liaodong, yet you are placing the Turks south of the river not far from the capital — how can one fail to worry about future troubles!
translations.idiomatic: All the ministers argued, "Your Majesty is about to launch a distant campaign in Liaodong, yet you are settling the Turks south of the Yellow River, not far from the capital. Surely we must reckon with what may come afterward!

sentences.zh: 願留鎮洛陽，遣諸將東征。」

translations.literal: We wish you would remain to guard Luoyang and send the generals east on the expedition."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that you remain to hold Luoyang and send the generals east on the campaign."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「夷狄亦人耳，其情與中夏不殊。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Barbarians too are only people; their feelings do not differ from those of the Central Lands.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The barbarians too are human beings; their hearts are no different from those of the Central Lands.

sentences.zh: 人主患德澤不加，不必猜忌異類。

translations.literal: What a ruler should worry about is that his grace and kindness do not reach them — there is no need to suspect those of other kinds.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's concern should be that his grace and kindness fail to reach them, not that he must distrust those who differ from him.

sentences.zh: 蓋德澤洽，則四夷可使如一家；

translations.literal: If grace and kindness pervade, then the four barbarian quarters can be made like one family;
translations.idiomatic: When grace and kindness suffuse the realm, the four quarters of barbarians can be made one household;

sentences.zh: 猜忌多，則骨肉不免為仇亂。

translations.literal: if suspicion is abundant, then even flesh and blood cannot escape becoming mutual enemies and rebels.
translations.idiomatic: when suspicion runs deep, even kin cannot escape turning into enemies and rebels.

sentences.zh: 煬帝無道，失人已久，遼東之役，人皆斷手足以避征役，玄感以運卒反於黎陽，非戎狄為患也。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was devoid of the Way and lost the people's hearts long ago; in the Liaodong campaign men all cut off hands and feet to avoid conscription; Xuansense raised transport conscripts in rebellion at Liyang — it was not the Rong and Di who brought calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang was without the Way and had long since lost the people's hearts. During the Liaodong campaign, men maimed themselves to escape conscription, and Yang Xuansense raised transport conscripts in revolt at Liyang. The danger did not come from the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 朕今征高麗，皆取願行者，募十得百，募百得千，其不得從軍者，皆憤歎鬱邑，豈比隋之行怨民哉！

translations.literal: Now in my Goguryeo campaign I take only willing volunteers — from ten recruited I get a hundred, from a hundred I get a thousand; those who could not join the army all sigh in indignation and resentment — how can this compare with the Sui's marching with a resentful people!
translations.idiomatic: In my campaign against Goguryeo I take only volunteers. For every ten I recruit, a hundred come forward; for every hundred, a thousand. Those who cannot join the army sigh in frustration and resentment. How can that compare with the Sui marching a people seething with grievance!

sentences.zh: 突厥貧弱，吾收而養之，計其感恩，入於骨髓，豈肯為患！

translations.literal: The Turks are poor and weak; I took them in and nourished them — calculating that their gratitude would enter into their marrow — how could they be willing to bring calamity!
translations.idiomatic: The Turks are poor and weak. I took them in and nourished them, expecting gratitude that would sink into their marrow. Why would they turn against us!

sentences.zh: 且彼與薛延陀嗜欲略同，彼不北走薛延陀而南歸我，其情可見矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, their desires are much the same as the Xueyantuo's; they did not flee north to Xueyantuo but returned south to us — their feelings can be seen."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, their appetites are much the same as the Xueyantuo's. They did not flee north to the Xueyantuo but came south to us — their inclinations are plain enough."

sentences.zh: 顧謂褚遂良曰：「爾知起居，為我志之，自今十五年，保無突厥之患。」

translations.literal: Turning, he said to Chu Suiliang: "You keep the diary of my acts — record this for me: from today, for fifteen years, I guarantee there will be no Turk trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Chu Suiliang, he said, "You keep the imperial diary. Record this for me: from today, for fifteen years, I guarantee there will be no trouble from the Turks."

sentences.zh: 俟利苾既失眾，輕騎入朝，上以為右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Qilibi, having lost his following, entered court with a light escort; the emperor made him General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost his following, Qilibi came to court with a small escort. The emperor appointed him General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，韋挺坐不先行視漕渠，運米六百餘艘至盧思台側，淺塞不能進，械送洛陽；

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Wei Ting was convicted because he had not gone ahead to inspect the canal; over six hundred rice-transport boats reached the side of Lusi Terrace but were blocked in the shallows and could not advance, and he was sent under restraint to Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Wei Ting was punished for failing to inspect the canal in advance. More than six hundred grain barges reached the banks of Lusi Terrace but ran aground in the shallows and could not proceed. He was sent to Luoyang in fetters.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，除名，以將作少監李道裕代之。

translations.literal: On dingyou he was stripped of rank; Li Daoyu, Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction, was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou he was dismissed from office. Li Daoyu, Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Construction, replaced him.

sentences.zh: 崔仁師亦坐免官。

translations.literal: Cui Renshi was likewise convicted and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Renshi was also dismissed from office on the same charge.

sentences.zh: 滄州刺史席辯坐贓污，二月，庚子，詔朝集使臨觀而戮之。

translations.literal: Cangzhou Prefect Xi Bian was convicted of corruption; in the second month, on gengzi, an edict ordered the provincial aggregators to attend and witness his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Bian, prefect of Cangzhou, was convicted of corruption. In the second month, on gengzi, an edict ordered the provincial aggregators to attend and witness his execution.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，上自將諸軍發洛陽，以特進蕭瑀為洛陽宮留守。

translations.literal: On gengxu the emperor personally led the armies out from Luoyang, appointing Tejin Xiao Yu to remain and guard the Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the emperor personally led the armies out from Luoyang, appointing Tejin Xiao Yu to remain as guardian of the Luoyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔：「朕發定州後，宜令皇太子監國。」

translations.literal: On yimao an edict said: "After I depart Dingzhou, the Crown Prince should be ordered to supervise the realm."
translations.idiomatic: On yimao an edict declared, "After I leave Dingzhou, the Crown Prince shall be ordered to oversee the realm."

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司致仕尉遲敬德上言：「陛下親征遼東，太子在定州，長安、洛陽心腹空虛，恐有玄感之變。

translations.literal: Retired Kaifu Yitong Sansi Yuchi Jingde submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty is personally campaigning in Liaodong; the Crown Prince is at Dingzhou; Chang'an and Luoyang, the heartlands, are empty — I fear there may be a Xuansense-style mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: The retired Kaifu Yitong Sansi Yuchi Jingde submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty is personally campaigning in Liaodong while the Crown Prince remains at Dingzhou. Chang'an and Luoyang, the heartlands, stand empty. I fear a revolt like Yang Xuansense's.

sentences.zh: 且邊隅小夷，不足以勤萬乘，願遣偏師征之，指期可殄。」

translations.literal: Moreover, a petty border tribe is not worth troubling the imperial chariot; I wish you would send a detached force against them — within a set term they can be exterminated."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a petty border tribe is not worth moving the imperial chariot. Send a detached force against them, and within a fixed term they can be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept the advice.

sentences.zh: 以敬德為左一馬軍總管，使從行。

translations.literal: He made Jingde Left First Horse-Army Commander-in-Chief and had him accompany the march.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Jingde Commander-in-Chief of the Left First Horse Army and had him accompany the campaign.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，詔謚殷太師比干曰忠列，所司封其墓，春秋祠以少牢，給隨近五戶供灑掃。

translations.literal: On dingsi an edict posthumously titled Yin Grand Master Bi Gan as Zhonglie; the responsible offices were to enclose his tomb; in spring and autumn sacrifice with a young ox was offered; five nearby households were granted to tend sweeping and sprinkling.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi an edict posthumously ennobled Yin Grand Master Bi Gan as Loyal and Upright. The responsible offices were to enclose his tomb, offer spring and autumn sacrifices with a young ox, and grant five nearby households to maintain it.

sentences.zh: 上之發京師也，命房玄齡得以便宜從事，不復奏請。

translations.literal: When the emperor set out from the capital, he ordered Fang Xuanling to act at his discretion without again submitting requests for approval.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor set out from the capital, he authorized Fang Xuanling to act at his discretion without submitting every matter for approval.

sentences.zh: 或詣留台稱有密，玄齡問密謀所在，對曰：「公則是也。」

translations.literal: Someone came to the rear secretariat claiming to have a secret; Xuanling asked where the secret plot lay, and the man replied: "You are it."
translations.idiomatic: Someone came to the rear secretariat claiming to possess a secret. Xuanling asked where the conspiracy lay. The man replied, "You are the conspirator."

sentences.zh: 玄齡驛送行在。

translations.literal: Xuanling sent him by relay post to the emperor's temporary residence.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling sent him by relay post to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 上聞留守有表送告密人，上怒，使人持長刀於前而後見之，問告者為誰，曰：「房玄齡。」

translations.literal: Hearing that the rear guard had sent a memorial forwarding an informer, the emperor was angry; he had a man hold a long saber in front and then receive him; asked who the informer accused, the man said: "Fang Xuanling."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned that the rear guard had forwarded the informer in a memorial, he was furious. He had a man hold a long saber before him and then received him. Asked whom he accused, the man said, "Fang Xuanling."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「果然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "As expected."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Just as I thought."

sentences.zh: 叱令腰斬。

translations.literal: He shouted an order to cut him at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him cut in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 璽書讓玄齡以不能自信，「更有如是者，可專決之。」

translations.literal: An imperial letter rebuked Xuanling for lacking self-confidence: "If there are more like this, you may decide on your own."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter rebuked Xuanling for lacking confidence: "If more such cases arise, you may decide them yourself."

sentences.zh: 癸亥，上至鄴，自為文祭魏太祖，曰：「臨危制變，料敵設奇，一將之智有餘，萬乘之才不足。」

translations.literal: On guihai the emperor reached Ye; he himself composed a text sacrificing to Cao Cao, Wei Founding Emperor, saying: "Facing danger and controlling change, estimating the enemy and deploying stratagem — as a general his wisdom was more than enough; as ruler of ten thousand chariots his talent was insufficient."
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the emperor reached Ye and himself composed a sacrificial text for Wei Founding Emperor Cao Cao, saying, "In crisis he adapted and changed course; he read the enemy and laid stratagems. As a general his wisdom was more than sufficient; as a ruler of ten thousand chariots his talent fell short."

sentences.zh: 是月，李世勣軍至幽州。

translations.literal: That month, Li Shiji's army reached Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That month Li Shiji's army reached Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁丑，車駕至定州。

translations.literal: Third month, dingchou — the imperial carriage reached Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingchou, the imperial carriage reached Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，上謂侍臣曰：「遼東本中國之地，隋氏四出師而不能得；

translations.literal: On dinghai the emperor told attendant ministers: "Liaodong was originally territory of China; the Sui dynasty sent out armies four times yet could not take it;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the emperor told his attendant ministers, "Liaodong was originally Chinese territory, yet the Sui sent armies four times and still could not take it.

sentences.zh: 朕今東征，欲為中國報子弟之仇，高麗雪君父之恥耳。

translations.literal: I now campaign east to avenge for China the wrong done its sons and younger brothers, and to wipe away the shame Goguryeo has brought upon sovereign and father.
translations.idiomatic: I campaign east now to avenge for China the deaths of its sons and brothers, and to wipe away the disgrace Goguryeo has inflicted upon our sovereign and fathers.

sentences.zh: 且方隅大定，惟此未平，故及朕之未老，用士大夫餘力以取之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the realm is largely settled — only this remains unconquered — so while I am not yet old, I use the surplus strength of scholar-officials and gentlemen to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the realm is largely settled and only this corner remains unconquered. While I am not yet old, I mean to use whatever strength the scholar-officials still have to take it.

sentences.zh: 朕自發洛陽，唯啖肉飯，雖春蔬亦不之進，懼其煩憂故也。」

translations.literal: Since I set out from Luoyang I have eaten only meat and rice; even spring vegetables I have not allowed — for fear of troubling and worrying the people."
translations.idiomatic: Since leaving Luoyang I have eaten only meat and rice. I have not even allowed spring vegetables, for fear of burdening the people."

sentences.zh: 上見病卒，召至御榻前存慰，付州縣療之，士卒莫不感悅。

translations.literal: When he saw sick soldiers, he summoned them before his couch to inquire and comfort, entrusted them to prefectures and counties for treatment — the troops were all moved and delighted.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw sick soldiers, he summoned them to his couch to inquire after them and entrusted them to the local prefectures and counties for treatment. The troops were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 有不預征名，自願以私裝從軍，動以千討，皆曰：「不求縣官勳賞，惟願效死遼東！」

translations.literal: There were those not on the draft rolls who volunteered with private equipment to join the army — often numbering in the thousands — all saying: "We seek no official honors or rewards; we only wish to die effecting service in Liaodong!"
translations.idiomatic: Men not on the draft rolls volunteered to join the army with their own equipment, often numbering in the thousands. All said, "We ask for no official honors or rewards — we only wish to die serving in Liaodong!"

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not allow it.

sentences.zh: 上將發，太子悲泣數日，上曰：「今留汝鎮守，輔以俊賢，欲使天下識汝風采。

translations.literal: About to set out, the Crown Prince wept sorrowfully for days; the emperor said: "Now I leave you to guard and hold the realm, assisted by outstanding worthies — I wish the realm to know your bearing.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to depart, the Crown Prince wept for days. The emperor said, "I leave you now to hold the realm, assisted by outstanding men of talent. I want the empire to see what you are made of.

sentences.zh: 夫為國之要，在於進賢退不肖，賞善罰惡，至公無私，汝當努力行此，悲泣何為！」

translations.literal: The essentials of governing a state lie in advancing the worthy and removing the unworthy, rewarding good and punishing evil, utmost fairness without partiality — you should strive to practice this; what is the use of weeping!"
translations.idiomatic: The essentials of governing lie in advancing the worthy and removing the unworthy, rewarding good and punishing evil, with utmost fairness and no partiality. Strive to do this. What good are tears!"

sentences.zh: 命開府儀同三司高士廉攝太子太傅，與劉洎、馬周、少詹事張行成、右庶子高季輔同掌機務，輔太子。

translations.literal: He appointed Kaifu Yitong Sansi Gao Shilian as acting Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, and together with Liu Ji, Ma Zhou, Junior Guardian Zhang Xingcheng, and Right Vice-Gentleman Gao Jifu to jointly manage state affairs and assist the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Kaifu Yitong Sansi Gao Shilian acting Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, and together with Liu Ji, Ma Zhou, Junior Guardian Zhang Xingcheng, and Right Vice-Gentleman Gao Jifu put them in charge of state affairs to assist the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌、岑文本與吏部尚書楊師道從行。

translations.literal: Changsun Wuji, Cen Wenben, and Minister of Personnel Yang Shidao accompanied the march.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Wuji, Cen Wenben, and Minister of Personnel Yang Shidao accompanied the campaign.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，車駕發定州，親佩弓矢，手結雨衣於鞍後。

translations.literal: On renchen the imperial carriage set out from Dingzhou; he personally wore bow and arrows and tied a rain cloak by hand behind the saddle.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the imperial carriage departed Dingzhou. The emperor personally wore bow and arrows and tied a rain cloak behind his saddle with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 命長孫元忌攝侍中，楊師道攝中書令。

translations.literal: He ordered Changsun Yuanji to act as Palace Attendant and Yang Shidao to act as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Changsun Yuanji to serve as acting Palace Attendant and Yang Shidao as acting Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 李世勣軍發柳城，多張形勢，若出懷遠鎮者，而潛師北趣甬道，出高麗不意。

translations.literal: Li Shiji's army set out from Liucheng, greatly displaying forces as though departing from Huaiyuan garrison, while secretly moving troops north toward the Yongdao route, catching Goguryeo off guard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji's army set out from Liucheng, making a great show as though heading from Huaiyuan garrison, while secretly marching north along the Yongdao route to take Goguryeo by surprise.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊戌朔，世勣自通定濟遼水，至玄菟。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, first day (wuxu): Shiji crossed the Liao River from Tongding and reached Xuantu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day (wuxu), Shiji crossed the Liao River from Tongding and reached Xuantu.

sentences.zh: 高麗大駭，城邑皆閉門自守。

translations.literal: Goguryeo was greatly alarmed; cities and towns all closed their gates and held themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo was thrown into panic. Cities and towns everywhere shut their gates and held fast.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，遼東道副大總管江夏王道宗將兵數千至新城，折衝都尉曹三良引十餘騎直壓城門，城中驚擾，無敢出者。

translations.literal: On renyin, Liaodong Route Assistant Grand Commander Prince Jiangxia Daozong led several thousand troops to Xincheng; Irregular-Cavalry Commander Cao Sanliang led a dozen-odd horsemen straight up to the city gate; inside the city there was alarm and turmoil, none daring to sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Assistant Grand Commander of the Liaodong Route, Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong, led several thousand men to Xincheng. Irregular-Cavalry Commander Cao Sanliang took a dozen horsemen straight to the city gate. Inside the city there was panic; no one dared come out.

sentences.zh: 營州都督張儉將胡兵為前鋒，進渡遼水，趨建安城，破高麗兵，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Yingzhou Protector-General Zhang Jian led Hu troops as vanguard, advanced, crossed the Liao River, hastened to Jian'an city, defeated Goguryeo troops, and beheaded several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou Protector-General Zhang Jian led Hu troops as vanguard, crossed the Liao River, pushed toward Jian'an city, defeated the Goguryeo army, and took several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 太子引高士廉同榻視事，又令更為士廉設案，士廉固辭。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince invited Gao Shilian to share a couch while conducting affairs, and again ordered a separate desk set for Shilian; Shilian firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince had Gao Shilian share his couch while conducting affairs, and again ordered a separate desk set out for Shilian. Shilian firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 丁未，車駕發幽州。

translations.literal: On dingwei the imperial carriage set out from Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the imperial carriage departed Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 上悉以軍中資糧、器械、簿書委岑文本，文本鳳夜勤力，躬自料配，籌、筆不去手，精神耗竭，言辭舉措，頗異平日。

translations.literal: The emperor entrusted all army provisions, weapons, and registers to Cen Wenben; Wenben toiled day and night, personally tallying and allocating; counting-rods and brush never left his hand; his spirit was exhausted; his speech and conduct were quite unlike ordinary days.
